optionWhy: Hybrid delivery combines iterative-incremental and linear-sequential ways of delivering products.
Linear-sequential alone does not describe the software iterations.
A temporary project can use several delivery methods without becoming operations.
Tailoring can support different methods within the same project.

questions.stem: A team says its project will never end because the new service will operate for years. What is the key misunderstanding?
options: The project can close when its products are accepted even while operations and benefits continue
A project may not close until every benefit is realized
A project ends the instant its business case is first approved
Any long-lived product makes the project permanent
questions.why: The project is temporary; the resulting service and post-project benefits may continue long afterward.
optionWhy: The project is temporary; the resulting service and post-project benefits may continue long afterward.
Some benefits are deliberately measured after the project closes.
Business-case approval authorizes work; it does not itself finish the project.
Product lifetime and project lifetime are different things.

questions.stem: Before committing to another stage, the board checks whether costs and anticipated benefits still justify continuing. Which principle is most directly visible?
questions.why: The decision tests whether the project continues to be worthwhile for the business.
optionWhy: The decision tests whether the project continues to be worthwhile for the business.
Product focus clarifies deliverables and quality rather than economic justification.
Exception management delegates within tolerance; the core clue here is continued value.
Lessons may inform the decision, but the actual check is justification.

questions.stem: A project manager retrieves a lessons report from a similar rollout before selecting a supplier. Which principle is illustrated?
questions.why: Using relevant previous lessons before making decisions applies learn from experience.
optionWhy: Using relevant previous lessons before making decisions applies learn from experience.
Stage management concerns planning and control at authorization boundaries.
Tailoring concerns adapting the method to circumstances, not simply reusing lessons.
Defined responsibilities clarify accountability, not the use of historical learning.

questions.stem: A project board authorizes the manager to spend within a cost range without asking for every minor decision. What makes this possible?
options: Manage by exception with delegated tolerances
Manage by stages with no delegated authority
Focus on products without quality criteria
Tailor away the approval process entirely
questions.why: Tolerances define the manager’s decision boundary; forecast breaches are escalated.
optionWhy: Tolerances define the manager’s decision boundary; forecast breaches are escalated.
Stages create decision points but do not eliminate the need for tolerances.
Product focus requires quality criteria and does not define spending authority.
Tailoring simplifies controls but cannot remove the underlying exception principle.

questions.stem: A small internal project decides not to define who represents users. Which statement is correct?
options: The method should be tailored, but user interests and responsibilities still need clear representation
This is acceptable because the project is small
The project manager automatically replaces every project board role
Small projects do not have to justify their investment
questions.why: The PRINCE2 principles still apply, including defined roles, responsibilities and relationships.
optionWhy: The PRINCE2 principles still apply, including defined roles, responsibilities and relationships.
Scale permits simpler documents, not loss of essential accountability.
The manager is separate from the project board’s directing accountability.
Continued business justification applies regardless of size.

questions.stem: The team defines the acceptance criteria before building a new customer portal. Which principle is the strongest match?
questions.why: Clear product expectations and quality criteria come before detailed activities.
optionWhy: Clear product expectations and quality criteria come before detailed activities.
Tolerances concern delegated decision-making, not defining the product.
The scenario does not describe learning from earlier work.
Stages organize control points; the clue here is acceptance criteria.

questions.stem: Which statement describes appropriate tailoring of PRINCE2 7?
options: Terminology and detail can be adapted while every principle still applies
A riskier project may discard the risk practice
The executive alone may remove principles to reduce paperwork
Tailoring is performed only after the project has closed
questions.why: Tailoring fits the method to the context without discarding its principles.
optionWhy: Tailoring fits the method to the context without discarding its principles.
The risk practice still needs to be addressed on a PRINCE2 project.
A single role cannot remove core PRINCE2 principles.
Tailoring is considered early and kept under review as the project changes.

questions.stem: Users fear that a new system will change their daily tasks. Which action best addresses the people element?
options: Engage affected people and plan the transition to new ways of working
Treat all resistance as an off-specification
Wait for final acceptance before discussing the change
Ask only the technical supplier to define user adoption
questions.why: People and organizational change require engagement, support and feedback throughout delivery.
optionWhy: People and organizational change require engagement, support and feedback throughout delivery.
An off-specification concerns a product failing requirements, not routine change resistance.
Late engagement risks poor adoption and lost benefits.
Suppliers supply expertise but cannot solely represent user needs or adoption.

questions.stem: A team holds workshops where operational users shape the proposed solution. What is this best described as?
questions.why: Co-creation invites those affected by the change to help shape what is delivered.
optionWhy: Co-creation invites those affected by the change to help shape what is delivered.
An exception plan replaces a plan after a forecast tolerance breach.
A checkpoint report communicates work-package progress at agreed intervals.
Independent audit is quality assurance, not collaborative design.

questions.stem: Which information belongs primarily in the communication management approach?
options: Who needs information, the channels, frequency and feedback arrangements
The detailed quality criteria for a specialist product
The current status of each issue in the issue register
The board’s decision on a particular exception report
questions.why: The approach defines how two-way communication with stakeholders is managed.
optionWhy: The approach defines how two-way communication with stakeholders is managed.
Product quality criteria are described in product specifications/descriptions.
Individual issue statuses belong in the project log/issue register.
An exception decision is a project control decision, not the overarching communications approach.

questions.stem: An employee outside the project team says the outcome will disrupt their job. Are they a stakeholder?
options: Yes, because a stakeholder may be affected without holding a project role
No, only members of the project board are stakeholders
Only if they approve the business case
Only if they work for an external supplier
questions.why: Stakeholders can affect or be affected by the project, including people outside the management team.
optionWhy: Stakeholders can affect or be affected by the project, including people outside the management team.
The board represents key interests but is not the full set of stakeholders.
Formal decision authority is not required to be a stakeholder.
Stakeholders may be internal or external.

questions.stem: A temporary cross-organization team is struggling with trust and different working cultures. What should its leader do?
options: Build shared ways of working and support team cohesion
Ignore the differences because relationships are not examinable
Delegate all culture problems to the risk owner
Remove user representatives to reduce debate
questions.why: Leading successful teams includes cultural awareness, collaboration and social cohesion.
optionWhy: Leading successful teams includes cultural awareness, collaboration and social cohesion.
People and relationships are a named integrated element of PRINCE2 7.
A risk owner manages assigned risk, not all human relationship issues.
User engagement matters to acceptance and benefit realization.

questions.stem: Which distinction is most helpful when reading a scenario about organizational adoption?
options: Change management helps people transition; issue/change control governs modifications to baselines
Change management and issue control are identical
A request for change always means users dislike the new system
The project should ignore stakeholder feedback until after closure
questions.why: People-focused change management differs from control of requests to modify approved baselines.
optionWhy: People-focused change management differs from control of requests to modify approved baselines.
They operate in different areas, although they may interact.
A request for change is a proposal to alter a baseline, not necessarily a complaint.
Feedback should be planned and used throughout the project.

questions.stem: A project delivers new booking software, and customers then begin booking online. What is the customers’ new behaviour?
questions.why: The new pattern of behaviour enabled by the product is an outcome.
optionWhy: The new pattern of behaviour enabled by the product is an outcome.
The software itself is an output; it enables the behaviour change.
A management approach defines how benefits are pursued and checked, not the changed behaviour.
A risk budget funds actions addressing uncertainty, not the achieved change.

questions.stem: Online bookings reduce call-centre costs by €30,000 annually. What is that quantified improvement?
questions.why: A measurable improvement resulting from an outcome is a benefit.
optionWhy: A measurable improvement resulting from an outcome is a benefit.
An output is the delivered specialist product, such as booking software.
A dis-benefit is a measurable negative consequence.
A mandate triggers work; it is not the improvement created by delivery.

questions.stem: A new self-service portal saves money but increases accessibility complaints. What is the increase in complaints?
questions.why: A measurable negative consequence of the change may be recorded as a dis-benefit.
optionWhy: A measurable negative consequence of the change may be recorded as a dis-benefit.
A portal is an output; complaints are a consequence of adoption.
Cost tolerance governs permitted financial variation.
A stage boundary is a management decision point, not a negative outcome.

questions.stem: Who has ultimate accountability for the business case and the investment justification?
questions.why: The executive represents the business interest and is accountable for the business case.
optionWhy: The executive represents the business interest and is accountable for the business case.
The senior user specifies needs and benefits from the user perspective.
The manager develops and maintains information for decisions but is not the project’s single business accountability.
Project support offers administrative help and does not own the justification.

questions.stem: Which management product describes how and when expected benefits will be measured?
questions.why: The benefits management approach sets benefit review actions, responsibilities and timing.
optionWhy: The benefits management approach sets benefit review actions, responsibilities and timing.
The business case justifies the investment using estimated benefits, costs and risks.
A product description defines a specific deliverable’s characteristics and quality.
A highlight report provides regular project progress to the board.

questions.stem: The project board checks the business case before approving a new delivery stage. Why?
options: To confirm that continuing the project still makes sense
To replace the independent assurance function
To prove every benefit has already been realized
To approve every individual work package
questions.why: Investment justification must be maintained and reviewed during project life.
optionWhy: Investment justification must be maintained and reviewed during project life.
Reviewing justification does not replace project assurance responsibilities.
Some benefits can only be measured after delivery or closure.
Work packages are normally authorized by the project manager, not individually by the board.

questions.stem: A team is selecting between two alternative ways to deliver the same outcomes. Which practice primarily establishes the investment case for the preferred option?
questions.why: The business case evaluates business options and whether the preferred approach is worth investing in.
optionWhy: The business case evaluates business options and whether the preferred approach is worth investing in.
Quality defines and verifies required product fitness for purpose.
Progress monitors performance against planned targets.
Risk assesses uncertainty, which informs the business case but is not the whole investment decision.

questions.stem: The board has delegated delivery work to the project manager. Which person normally agrees the work package directly with the manager?
questions.why: The team manager accepts and delivers agreed work packages from the project manager.
optionWhy: The team manager accepts and delivers agreed work packages from the project manager.
The executive chairs business accountability at directing level.
Project assurance independently checks the project for board members.
The senior user represents the needs of users and benefits.

questions.stem: A specialist lead forecasts that an agreed work package will exceed its time tolerance. Who should receive the escalation?
questions.why: The team manager raises the work-package issue to the project manager for decision.
optionWhy: The team manager raises the work-package issue to the project manager for decision.
The business layer sets project-level constraints and is not the routine work-package escalatee.
The board normally receives stage-level exceptions from the project manager.
Independent quality assurance does not control work-package tolerance decisions.

questions.stem: Who represents the supplier perspective and is accountable for technical integrity?
questions.why: The senior supplier represents delivery expertise and supplier resources and quality.
optionWhy: The senior supplier represents delivery expertise and supplier resources and quality.
The senior user represents the recipient community and expected benefits.
The executive owns the business case and overall business accountability.
Project support provides services such as planning administration and record keeping.

questions.stem: Why must project assurance remain separate from the project manager?
options: To preserve independent assessment on behalf of the project board
Because assurance approves every team plan
Because assurance sets all project-level tolerances
questions.why: The project board must be assured independently of the person managing the work.
optionWhy: The project board must be assured independently of the person managing the work.
Team plans are generally controlled by team managers and agreed with the project manager.
Assurance examines interests; it does not supply the specialist team.
The business layer sets project tolerances; the board sets stage tolerances.

questions.stem: A small project’s manager also directly leads the specialist team. Is this always forbidden?
options: No, the project manager may also perform the team manager role when appropriate
Yes, all PRINCE2 roles must be held by different people
Yes, because the project manager must also be the executive
No, because the board no longer needs to exist
questions.why: PRINCE2 allows some roles to be combined; managing and delivering may be combined with suitable skills.
optionWhy: PRINCE2 allows some roles to be combined; managing and delivering may be combined with suitable skills.
Tailoring permits some role combination without losing required responsibilities.
The executive must remain separate from the project manager.
The project board remains the directing authority.

questions.stem: Who establishes the project-level tolerances within which the project board operates?
questions.why: The organization/business layer commissions the project and sets its overall tolerances.
optionWhy: The organization/business layer commissions the project and sets its overall tolerances.
The project manager is given stage tolerances by the project board.
The team manager works within agreed work-package tolerances.
Project support does not set project authority limits.

questions.stem: The board delegates authority to decide certain changes up to an agreed budget. What role is receiving that authority?
questions.why: A change authority may approve specified change decisions within delegated limits.
optionWhy: A change authority may approve specified change decisions within delegated limits.
Assurance independently checks the project and does not automatically approve changes.
Support provides administrative services rather than approving change by default.
A risk action owner performs assigned risk-response actions, not change approvals.

questions.stem: The board wants to understand the main products, schedule and budget for the entire project. Which plan is primarily relevant?
questions.why: The project plan outlines the overall delivery and major targets across the project.
optionWhy: The project plan outlines the overall delivery and major targets across the project.
The team plan organizes delivery of a specific work package.
An exception plan replaces an existing plan when an exception decision requires it.
A product description specifies a product, not the overall project schedule and budget.

questions.stem: A project manager needs sufficiently detailed control information for the next management stage. What should be prepared?
questions.why: The stage plan provides the basis for detailed day-to-day stage management.
optionWhy: The stage plan provides the basis for detailed day-to-day stage management.
A mandate authorizes pre-project investigation.
A benefits management approach defines benefit realization reviews.
A risk register contains risk records, not the whole stage schedule.

questions.stem: The team leader needs to schedule the tasks for their assigned work package. Which plan may be useful?
questions.why: Team plans are optional but support organizing and controlling a team’s work package.
optionWhy: Team plans are optional but support organizing and controlling a team’s work package.
The project plan does not usually provide team-level execution detail.
A business case addresses investment justification.
An end project report evaluates performance at closure, not team scheduling.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an exception plan?
options: It is prepared to replace a plan when the relevant authority requests a response to an exception
It is the mandatory first plan written for a project
It describes how to communicate with stakeholders
It records the results of every quality check
questions.why: An exception plan may replace a project or stage plan following an exception decision.
optionWhy: An exception plan may replace a project or stage plan following an exception decision.
An initiation stage plan is prepared during starting up a project.
The communication management approach covers stakeholder communication.
The quality register records planned and completed quality activities.

questions.stem: Which action comes first in product-based planning?
options: Define and analyse the required products
Assign every specialist activity a person before defining products
questions.why: Product-based planning starts with understanding the outputs and their interdependencies.
optionWhy: Product-based planning starts with understanding the outputs and their interdependencies.
Activities and resources are derived after clarifying what must be created.
The end stage report is produced at a stage boundary, not as the first planning step.
Change control is used for proposed modifications, not as the universal first planning activity.

questions.stem: A project team asks what shows the hierarchy of products required by a plan. Which technique output provides that?
questions.why: A product breakdown structure groups products in a hierarchy.
optionWhy: A product breakdown structure groups products in a hierarchy.
A product flow diagram shows sequence and dependency between products.
A highlight report communicates progress at agreed intervals.
A project mandate triggers the starting up activity.

questions.stem: A diagram shows that the test environment must exist before the application can be validated. What does it illustrate?
questions.why: A product flow diagram highlights which products are needed before others.
optionWhy: A product flow diagram highlights which products are needed before others.
The executive owns the investment justification rather than product sequence.
Assurance responsibilities are organizational, not product dependencies.
Risk appetite defines an attitude toward taking risk.

questions.stem: A product description lists the tests a new data extract must pass. What are those tests?
questions.why: Product descriptions specify expected quality and how it is checked.
optionWhy: Product descriptions specify expected quality and how it is checked.
An exception report describes forecast breaches of delegated tolerances.
A risk budget is money for risk responses, not a test specification.
A mandate explains the reason to explore a possible project.

questions.stem: A product is delivered but fails its agreed acceptance criterion. What should the team do?
options: Record the quality result and resolve the nonconformance through the appropriate control arrangements
Mark the product accepted because it was delivered on schedule
Move the failure into the benefits management approach
Stop quality checking all other products
questions.why: Quality checks establish whether products meet their specifications; failed criteria require action.
optionWhy: Quality checks establish whether products meet their specifications; failed criteria require action.
Being on time does not override the requirement for fitness for purpose.
Benefits management concerns outcomes and benefit measures, not detailed product failures.
A failure on one item does not justify abandoning control of all others.

questions.stem: What is the difference between quality assurance and project assurance?
options: Quality assurance is typically independent of the project; project assurance represents board interests within project governance
Project assurance is the same as the team’s quality test
Quality assurance always reports directly to the team manager
Neither should be independent of the project manager
questions.why: Organizational quality assurance and project board assurance are related but different functions.
optionWhy: Organizational quality assurance and project board assurance are related but different functions.
Quality control tests products; project assurance checks from a governance perspective.
Quality assurance is not supervised by the team manager as a delivery task.
Both forms of assurance should maintain appropriate independence.

questions.stem: Where would you expect to find scheduled and completed quality checks for project products?
questions.why: The quality register tracks quality activities and their results.
optionWhy: The quality register tracks quality activities and their results.
The risk register tracks identified uncertainty and responses.
The business case assesses investment justification.
The communication approach defines stakeholder information needs.

questions.stem: Which statement about acceptance criteria is most accurate?
options: They describe what the overall project product must satisfy to be accepted
They are the same as work-package cost tolerances
They are used only when the project has closed prematurely
They replace all individual product quality specifications
questions.why: Acceptance criteria define the conditions for customer/user acceptance of the project product.
optionWhy: Acceptance criteria define the conditions for customer/user acceptance of the project product.
Cost tolerances limit financial deviations, not acceptance.
Acceptance criteria are normally identified early and used during closing.
Individual products also need their own quality requirements.

questions.stem: A requirement changes after a product has been approved as the baseline. Which practice deals with the request for modification?
questions.why: The Issues practice controls requests to alter approved baselines, even if discovered during quality work.
optionWhy: The Issues practice controls requests to alter approved baselines, even if discovered during quality work.
Quality control tests conformance and may raise an issue, but does not bypass change control.
Business-case impact may be assessed, but the procedure is issue management.
People/change adoption is distinct from approved-baseline control.

questions.stem: A team begins writing a solution without agreeing what “fit for purpose” means. What is the key risk?
options: Quality expectations and criteria are not yet agreed
The board has used too many management stages
Every risk is automatically an issue
questions.why: Quality planning requires a clear specification of what success looks like before verification.
optionWhy: Quality planning requires a clear specification of what success looks like before verification.
Stage length is a separate planning question.
Risk remains an uncertain possibility until a relevant event occurs; the terms are not interchangeable.
The scenario describes planning shortcomings, not closure.

questions.stem: A port strike has not happened, but it could delay equipment delivery. How should the possibility be classified?
options: A confirmed issue with no uncertainty
questions.why: An uncertain future event that could harm objectives is a threat risk.
optionWhy: An uncertain future event that could harm objectives is a threat risk.
An off-specification means a product will not meet its approved specification.
A confirmed incident would be an issue; the strike has not occurred.
A benefit is a measurable advantage from an outcome.

questions.stem: A risk is expected to occur around the final delivery week. Which attribute describes its position in time?
questions.why: Proximity describes when a risk might occur.
optionWhy: Proximity describes when a risk might occur.
Velocity describes how quickly the effect follows the event.
Exposure describes how much an objective is at risk overall.
Appetite describes how much and what kinds of risk the business is willing to take.

questions.stem: A cyber incident could disrupt operations within minutes if it occurs. Which risk attribute is described by the rapid onset of effects?
questions.why: Velocity is the speed with which the impact follows the risk event.
optionWhy: Velocity is the speed with which the impact follows the risk event.
Proximity concerns how near the event itself is in time.
Risk budget pays for defined response actions.
Risk tolerance defines the acceptable range of exposure.

questions.stem: Which person is accountable for monitoring and controlling an assigned uncertainty over time?
questions.why: The risk owner is accountable for the risk and its overall response.
optionWhy: The risk owner is accountable for the risk and its overall response.
The risk action owner performs specific assigned response actions; they are not necessarily the risk owner.
Support may maintain records but is not automatically accountable for each risk.
Change authority approves specified changes, not all risk management.

questions.stem: A mitigation task is assigned to the network engineer while the operations lead retains accountability for the overall risk. Who is the engineer?
options: The executive solely because there is a budget
questions.why: The risk action owner carries out nominated response tasks.
optionWhy: The risk action owner carries out nominated response tasks.
The executive owns the business case, not automatically a technical task.
Product approval concerns quality acceptance, not risk implementation.
The operations lead still owns the overall risk in this scenario.

questions.stem: A favorable exchange rate might lower procurement costs. Which response aims to make that upside more likely or greater?
questions.why: Enhance increases the probability or benefit of an opportunity.
optionWhy: Enhance increases the probability or benefit of an opportunity.
Avoid seeks to remove a threat.
Transfer shares some threat impact with a third party, such as through insurance.
Reduce addresses threats, not positive opportunities.

questions.stem: Which sequence is consistent with the PRINCE2 7 risk-management technique?
options: Identify, assess, plan, implement, with communication throughout
Only log risks after they have happened
Start with an exception report for every possible risk
questions.why: Risk management cycles through identifying, assessing, planning and implementing, with communication.
optionWhy: Risk management cycles through identifying, assessing, planning and implementing, with communication.
These are not the named risk technique activities.
Recorded risks concern uncertain future events, not just occurred events.
An exception report is used for forecast tolerance breaches, not every risk.

questions.stem: A customer requests an additional reporting feature after the agreed product baseline has been approved. What type of issue is this?
questions.why: A proposal to alter an approved baseline is a request for change.
optionWhy: A proposal to alter an approved baseline is a request for change.
A risk is an uncertain event that may affect objectives.
A benefit is a measurable improvement, not a proposed feature.
A checkpoint report communicates work-package progress at intervals.

questions.stem: Tests show that a delivered component will not meet its quality specification. Which issue label fits?
questions.why: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its approved quality specifications.
optionWhy: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its approved quality specifications.
Proximity locates a future risk in time.
Manage by stages is a principle, not an issue type.
A highlight report is regular project reporting to the board.

questions.stem: The team reports a minor day-to-day concern that the manager can resolve informally. Where can it initially be recorded?
questions.why: Informal issues can be captured in the daily log within the project log.
optionWhy: Informal issues can be captured in the daily log within the project log.
The business case is an investment justification, not an informal issue diary.
An exception plan follows a management decision about a tolerance breach.
A project product description contains acceptance expectations for the project product.

questions.stem: A proposed baseline change is beyond the manager’s delegated change authority. Who needs to make the approval decision?
options: The project board or the authority to which that decision has properly been delegated
Any team member who identifies it
The senior supplier acting alone in every case
questions.why: Change decisions must follow agreed delegated authority limits, ultimately under the project board.
optionWhy: Change decisions must follow agreed delegated authority limits, ultimately under the project board.
Support may record the issue but does not automatically approve changes.
The person reporting a change does not automatically have approval rights.
The supplier role alone does not inherently approve all project baseline changes.

questions.stem: Which sequence best describes the main issue-management decision cycle?
options: Plan, direct, close, then define the issue
Record only, because all issues resolve themselves
Approve first and analyse after delivery
questions.why: The issue-management technique captures and assesses an issue before recommending, deciding and implementing a response.
optionWhy: The issue-management technique captures and assesses an issue before recommending, deciding and implementing a response.
Project processes do not replace the issue-management technique.
Issues may need proportionate decisions and follow-up actions.
An approval should follow impact analysis, not automatically precede it.

questions.stem: A quality defect is accepted without correction by an authorized decision-maker. What is this acceptance called?
questions.why: A concession is a decision to accept an off-specification without corrective action.
optionWhy: A concession is a decision to accept an off-specification without corrective action.
Exploit is a risk response to an opportunity.
A stage plan schedules and controls one management stage.
The mandate starts pre-project investigation.

questions.stem: A team manager sends its weekly status to the project manager. Which management report is most likely?
questions.why: A checkpoint report summarizes work-package progress from delivering to managing level.
optionWhy: A checkpoint report summarizes work-package progress from delivering to managing level.
A highlight report goes from the project manager to the board.
An end project report evaluates the whole project at closure.
An exception report explains a forecast tolerance breach needing higher authority.

questions.stem: Every month the project manager updates the board on stage progress. What report is this?
questions.why: Highlight reports provide periodic progress information from the project manager to the board.
optionWhy: Highlight reports provide periodic progress information from the project manager to the board.
Checkpoint reports normally come from the team manager to the project manager.
The risk approach defines how risks will be managed, not periodic board status.
An end stage report is event-driven at a stage boundary.

questions.stem: A work package will exceed its agreed effort limit, but the stage can still remain within its own tolerance. What should happen first?
options: The team manager raises an issue to the project manager for a decision
The team manager sends an exception report directly to business management
The board must automatically close the project
The team quietly adjusts the approved work package baseline
questions.why: The team escalates a forecast work-package deviation to the project manager, who can decide within stage authority.
optionWhy: The team escalates a forecast work-package deviation to the project manager, who can decide within stage authority.
An exception report goes from project manager to board for stage-level exceptions.
A local work-package deviation does not automatically require closure.
Baselines must be changed through control, not quietly rewritten.

questions.stem: The current stage is forecast to exceed its authorized cost tolerance. What is the project manager expected to produce?
options: An exception report to the project board
A revised baseline without telling the board
questions.why: A forecast stage-level tolerance breach is escalated through an exception report.
optionWhy: A forecast stage-level tolerance breach is escalated through an exception report.
Checkpoint reports are team-to-project-manager and do not replace escalation.
The project manager cannot silently exceed delegated stage authority.
Closure is not automatically the appropriate response to a stage exception.

questions.stem: Which type of control is a planned weekly checkpoint report?
questions.why: A report scheduled at regular calendar intervals is time-driven.
optionWhy: A report scheduled at regular calendar intervals is time-driven.
Event-driven controls respond to a defined occurrence such as a stage end.
Product acceptance is an outcome of quality control and may be a milestone.
Exception reports arise from forecast breaches rather than a weekly schedule.

questions.stem: Which of these is an event-driven control?
options: A review at the end of a management stage
questions.why: A stage-end authorization point is triggered by a milestone/event rather than a calendar frequency.
optionWhy: A stage-end authorization point is triggered by a milestone/event rather than a calendar frequency.
Weekly updates happen at predefined time intervals.
Monthly highlight reporting is time-driven.
A regular daily meeting is time-driven.

questions.stem: An exception plan is approved to replace the current stage plan. Who approves that replacement?
questions.why: The project board directs how a stage-level exception is resolved and approves the replacement plan.
optionWhy: The project board directs how a stage-level exception is resolved and approves the replacement plan.
The team manager manages work-package delivery and has no stage authorization role.
Support assists administration and may circulate documents but does not authorize the plan.
A risk action owner completes specific responses and does not authorize stages.

questions.stem: The project mandate has arrived, but detailed investment has not been authorized. What process checks that a worthwhile project can be initiated?
questions.why: Starting up a project tests the prerequisites and develops an initial brief before initiation authorization.
optionWhy: Starting up a project tests the prerequisites and develops an initial brief before initiation authorization.
Closing confirms acceptance and completes or prematurely ends the project.
Managing product delivery governs work packages between manager and teams.
Controlling a stage manages authorized stage work after initiation.

questions.stem: A project board must decide whether to fund initiation and later whether to authorize delivery. What overarching process covers its decisions?
questions.why: Directing a project provides board-level authorization and decisions throughout the lifecycle.
optionWhy: Directing a project provides board-level authorization and decisions throughout the lifecycle.
Managing product delivery is the manager-to-team interface.
Controlling a stage is the manager’s stage control process.
Starting up prepares an initial proposal but does not itself authorize board decisions.

questions.stem: The manager prepares the detailed business case, project plan and management approaches before major commitment. Which process?
questions.why: Initiating establishes the sound delivery and governance baseline presented through the PID.
optionWhy: Initiating establishes the sound delivery and governance baseline presented through the PID.
Closing reviews outcomes and acceptance after delivery.
Managing product delivery concerns team work packages.
Directing makes the board’s authorization decisions rather than preparing all the PID content.

questions.stem: The manager authorizes work packages, monitors issues and sends regular progress to the board. Which process is in use?
questions.why: Controlling a stage covers assigning work, tracking progress and corrective action inside a stage.
optionWhy: Controlling a stage covers assigning work, tracking progress and corrective action inside a stage.
Managing a stage boundary prepares review/approval of the next stage.
Starting up is pre-project preparation.
Closing evaluates final acceptance and shutdown.

questions.stem: A team manager accepts agreed work, creates products and returns completed packages. Which process governs that relationship?
questions.why: Managing product delivery formalizes agreement, execution and handback of work packages.
optionWhy: Managing product delivery formalizes agreement, execution and handback of work packages.
Directing describes project board governance.
Initiating creates the PID and baseline for implementation.
Closing confirms project acceptance and completion.

questions.stem: An end-stage report and next stage plan are prepared for a board decision. Which process provides this material?
questions.why: The manager uses managing a stage boundary to review performance and seek next-stage approval.
optionWhy: The manager uses managing a stage boundary to review performance and seek next-stage approval.
Controlling a stage handles current delivery but not the whole boundary decision package.
Starting up plans only initiation preparation before project authorization.
Product delivery is the work package interface, not stage authorization preparation.

questions.stem: The project product is accepted and operations has taken responsibility for support. Which process confirms project completion?
questions.why: Closing a project confirms acceptance, handover, performance and remaining follow-up actions.
optionWhy: Closing a project confirms acceptance, handover, performance and remaining follow-up actions.
Starting up explores whether a project should be initiated.
Managing product delivery completes team work, not overall project closure.
Initiating prepares the PID to request authorization for delivery.

questions.stem: The project is stopped early because the business case is no longer justified. What should still happen?
options: Orderly premature closure, including handover and unresolved-action arrangements
No closure process because the original products are incomplete
Automatic approval of all incomplete deliverables
Erase all issue and risk records
questions.why: PRINCE2 supports controlled premature closure rather than abandoning the project.
optionWhy: PRINCE2 supports controlled premature closure rather than abandoning the project.
A cancelled project still needs orderly closure decisions and documented follow-up.
Acceptance cannot be assumed for products that were not completed.
Open issues and risks may require follow-on action and retention of records.

questions.stem: The project board receives an exception report and asks for a replacement stage plan. Which process prepares that plan for review?
questions.why: Managing a stage boundary may prepare an exception plan for board consideration.
optionWhy: Managing a stage boundary may prepare an exception plan for board consideration.
Team-level work package delivery does not authorize a replacement stage plan.
Starting up occurs before initiation, not during an in-flight exception.
People/change adoption is not the named process for replacing a baseline plan.

questions.stem: Which process normally spans most of the project life because the board keeps giving direction at key points?
questions.why: Directing provides overall board control and key authorizations across the project lifecycle.
optionWhy: Directing provides overall board control and key authorizations across the project lifecycle.
Starting up is a short pre-project preparation process.
Closing is concentrated at the end or premature end.
Managing a stage boundary occurs at review points rather than continuously.

questions.stem: A council delivers a one-off replacement of its permit system, then returns to normal operations. What makes this work a project?
options: It is temporary and introduces a change through defined products
questions.why: The finite organization and intended change are project characteristics, unlike a permanent operational service.
optionWhy: A technical product does not by itself distinguish a project from day-to-day operations.
Projects and business-as-usual work can both have managers; the temporary change is decisive.
Performance measures apply equally to ongoing operations; they do not define a project.
The finite organization and intended change are project characteristics, unlike a permanent operational service.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A construction team completes foundations, then walls, then roofing, with each phase depending on completion of the previous one. Which delivery approach does this describe?
questions.why: A linear-sequential approach creates products in a largely fixed order, using earlier outputs before later work begins.
optionWhy: A linear-sequential approach creates products in a largely fixed order, using earlier outputs before later work begins.
An iterative-incremental approach cycles through learning and development in repeated increments.
A hybrid approach combines different delivery methods rather than using only a sequential pattern.
Time-driven control is scheduled monitoring at set intervals, not a method for creating products.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A flood-defence project builds barriers in a fixed order while releasing its resident-alert app through several feedback-led increments. What delivery approach fits the project?
questions.why: Hybrid delivery combines sequential construction with iterative-incremental software releases within one project.
optionWhy: A temporary flood-defence project creates an agreed change, irrespective of the delivery approach.
Hybrid delivery combines sequential construction with iterative-incremental software releases within one project.
The alert app changes over several increments, so a purely linear-sequential label misses that part.
The barriers are delivered in a fixed order, so not all work is iterative-incremental.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: An organization wants to use PRINCE2 for a small charity event and a multinational construction programme. Which characteristic of PRINCE2 supports both?
options: The seven principles are optional for small projects
The method is tailored to the project context
Every management product must be a separate long document
questions.why: PRINCE2 can be adapted to scale, complexity, commercial context, delivery approach and capabilities.
optionWhy: All seven principles still apply; their implementation may be proportionate.
PRINCE2 is intended for different industries and project types, not only construction.
PRINCE2 can be adapted to scale, complexity, commercial context, delivery approach and capabilities.
Tailoring can combine or simplify management products without abandoning the method.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A board discovers that a technically successful project no longer delivers value for money. Which principle should govern the next decision?
questions.why: A project must remain worthwhile throughout its life, not merely be technically achievable.
optionWhy: Product focus clarifies deliverables and acceptance; it does not replace a viable business rationale.
Lessons inform decisions, but the key issue is whether investment remains justified.
Stage boundaries provide review opportunities, while continued justification determines whether proceeding makes sense.
A project must remain worthwhile throughout its life, not merely be technically achievable.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The initiation team reviews the risks and successes of a similar project and changes its approach. Which principle is most directly demonstrated?
questions.why: Using relevant prior lessons to improve the current project is a direct application of learning from experience.
optionWhy: Using relevant prior lessons to improve the current project is a direct application of learning from experience.
Exception management concerns tolerances and delegated authority, not gathering previous lessons.
Product focus starts with what must be delivered and how acceptance will be demonstrated.
The project may also be tailored, but learning from prior experience is the activity stated.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The project board agrees that the senior user will represent beneficiaries and the senior supplier will represent technical delivery. Which principle is illustrated?
questions.why: This principle ensures business, user and supplier interests have clear representation and decision rights.
optionWhy: Reusing lessons may inform appointments, but explicit responsibilities are the central point.
This principle ensures business, user and supplier interests have clear representation and decision rights.
Stages define control periods; they do not define the representation of stakeholder interests.
Product descriptions specify deliverables rather than assigning governance interests.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The project board approves only the next three months of detailed delivery, leaving later work at high level. Which principle is most evident?
questions.why: PRINCE2 authorizes and controls work one management stage at a time, with appropriate detail for the near term.
optionWhy: Lessons could inform the plan, but the defining decision is approval of one management stage.
Product focus requires agreed outputs but does not alone dictate the timing of stage approvals.
PRINCE2 authorizes and controls work one management stage at a time, with appropriate detail for the near term.
Tolerances determine escalation limits; they do not themselves set the pattern of stage-by-stage authorization.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The project manager can spend up to an agreed limit without asking the board, but must escalate a forecast breach. Which principle allows this?
questions.why: Agreed tolerances define how much authority is delegated and when escalation becomes necessary.
optionWhy: Product focus concerns what must be created and accepted, not spending authority thresholds.
Using lessons can improve estimates but is not what sets tolerances.
Stage boundaries divide control periods; tolerances describe delegated authority within those periods.
Agreed tolerances define how much authority is delegated and when escalation becomes necessary.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A software project lists all outputs with measurable acceptance criteria before producing a detailed activity schedule. Which principle is foremost?
questions.why: The team first defines what is to be delivered and accepted before deciding how to perform the work.
optionWhy: The team first defines what is to be delivered and accepted before deciding how to perform the work.
No forecast breach or delegated tolerance is involved in this decision.
The question is about defining the required deliverables, not examining previous projects.
The business case explains why investment is worthwhile, whereas product focus clarifies delivery.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A tiny project combines two reporting documents into one concise document. What is the correct statement?
options: The project must copy every template exactly
Combining management products may be a valid tailoring choice if required information is retained
The project may omit manage by exception if it is small
The team can ignore the project board once the documents are combined
questions.why: Tailoring can simplify documentation to suit the project while preserving necessary governance information.
optionWhy: PRINCE2 supports proportionate adaptation rather than mandatory duplication of template structure.
Tailoring can simplify documentation to suit the project while preserving necessary governance information.
Project size does not allow any of the seven principles to be discarded.
Tailoring documents does not transfer or eliminate project board accountability.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which statement about tailoring to project conditions is correct?
options: Tailoring can only take place after closing a project
Tailoring concerns only which software tools are used
The application of PRINCE2 can be adjusted, but all principles remain applicable
Principles are optional if the project has fewer than ten people
questions.why: The method is adapted to the context; removing a principle would stop it being a genuinely PRINCE2-managed project.
optionWhy: Tailoring is considered when setting up and initiating the project and reviewed as circumstances change.
Tailoring can affect roles, processes, practices, control levels and management-product presentation.
The method is adapted to the context; removing a principle would stop it being a genuinely PRINCE2-managed project.
A small team affects the amount of formality needed, not whether the principles apply.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A project manager is asked to ignore a forecast tolerance breach until the next scheduled highlight report. Which principle is at risk?
questions.why: Forecast exceptions must be escalated promptly to the authority that set the tolerance; routine reporting does not replace escalation.
optionWhy: The problem is not failure to define products or their quality specifications.
A lessons review is valuable but cannot substitute for the required exception escalation.
Tailoring may alter reporting arrangements, but it cannot waive exception management.
Forecast exceptions must be escalated promptly to the authority that set the tolerance; routine reporting does not replace escalation.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A sponsor says that because requirements are fixed, the project need not review whether the business case remains sound. What is the best response?
options: Business justification must continue to be assessed even if product scope remains unchanged
Fixed scope proves the project remains desirable
The business case need only be checked after closure
The senior supplier can replace the business case with a quality checklist
questions.why: Economic and organizational circumstances can change independently of the approved product scope.
optionWhy: Economic and organizational circumstances can change independently of the approved product scope.
A fixed scope does not guarantee that benefits continue to outweigh costs and risks.
The business case supports investment decisions throughout the project, not just a post-project review.
Quality controls verify products; they cannot establish investment justification.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A new team has uncertainty about priorities. The project manager sets clear objectives, responsibilities and working rules. What is this principally?
questions.why: Management establishes work arrangements, objectives and control so that coordinated delivery can occur.
optionWhy: Issue resolution addresses relevant events and changes, not the basic setup of the team.
Management establishes work arrangements, objectives and control so that coordinated delivery can occur.
Leadership emphasizes motivating and influencing people; defining control structures and tasks is management.
Quality assurance provides independent confidence about standards and quality systems.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A team is losing motivation during an organizational transition. A leader influences, listens and inspires a shared purpose. Which concept is central?
questions.why: Leadership motivates and influences people and builds commitment, particularly where direct authority is limited.
optionWhy: Quality control checks whether products satisfy specifications.
Scheduling identifies when work should occur, rather than why people commit to it.
Leadership motivates and influences people and builds commitment, particularly where direct authority is limited.
Exception management defines escalation thresholds; it does not describe inspiring a team.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: An employee affected by a new payroll system has no formal project role. How should the project treat this person?
options: As a project board member automatically
As someone outside the scope of communication
As a supplier simply because they use software
As a stakeholder whose needs and feedback may matter
questions.why: Stakeholders include people affected by a project, whether or not they hold a position in its governance structure.
optionWhy: Being affected does not automatically confer a project board role or decision-making authority.
Affected staff can be important stakeholders and should not be excluded just because they are not project team members.
Using a product does not make an employee a supplier delivering specialist resources.
Stakeholders include people affected by a project, whether or not they hold a position in its governance structure.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A public-sector project has an internal project team and external residents impacted by its outcome. Which distinction matters?
options: People delivering the project and people affected by it may both require engagement
Only employees with project roles count as stakeholders
Only senior managers may influence adoption
Every affected person must be made a project manager
questions.why: PRINCE2 people guidance covers those working on change and those who experience its consequences.
optionWhy: PRINCE2 people guidance covers those working on change and those who experience its consequences.
Stakeholders may be outside the project team, and even outside the organization.
Operational users and other affected groups may strongly influence whether change succeeds.
Engagement does not require assigning each stakeholder a formal managerial role.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A project communicates its timetable to users but never asks whether it will disrupt essential services. What is missing?
questions.why: Effective engagement involves gathering reactions and feedback, not only sending one-way announcements.
optionWhy: Cost forecasts cannot substitute for understanding stakeholders affected by the change.
Effective engagement involves gathering reactions and feedback, not only sending one-way announcements.
Issue classification is useful but does not by itself collect user feedback.
An exception plan is needed for a forecast tolerance breach when requested, not for ordinary communication gaps.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which management product should describe how information is shared with stakeholders and feedback is received?
questions.why: The communication management approach defines the intended communication methods, timing, roles and feedback flows.
optionWhy: A quality register tracks planned and completed product quality activities.
An exception report escalates a forecast tolerance breach, rather than defining routine communications.
The communication management approach defines the intended communication methods, timing, roles and feedback flows.
A risk register tracks identified uncertainties and their status, not the full stakeholder communication arrangements.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A hospital team needs a plan for changing staff routines as a new clinical system goes live. Which management product is most relevant?
questions.why: The change management approach describes how affected people move from current to future ways of working.
optionWhy: The issue management approach controls issues and baseline changes, not the broader people transition.
Risks about adoption may be logged, but the register is not a complete people-transition approach.
The product register shows product status rather than arrangements for changing working practices.
The change management approach describes how affected people move from current to future ways of working.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Two departments jointly design a new customer journey, creating the solution together rather than handing off completed specifications. Which people concept is best illustrated?
questions.why: Co-creation involves people jointly shaping outcomes and producing value, rather than simply passing completed work between groups.
optionWhy: Co-creation involves people jointly shaping outcomes and producing value, rather than simply passing completed work between groups.
Exception planning replaces an approved plan after an exception decision; no such situation is described.
Periodic controls concern progress reporting intervals, not jointly creating a solution.
Independent assurance checks systems and standards rather than describing joint design activities.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Staff from different organizations work together on a shared plan while retaining separate responsibilities. What concept is being applied?
questions.why: Collaboration means working together towards agreed project goals, even where responsibilities remain distinct.
optionWhy: Escalation occurs when an issue or forecast exception needs attention from higher authority.
Collaboration means working together towards agreed project goals, even where responsibilities remain distinct.
Commercial authorization relates to agreed business commitments and contracts, not simply joint working.
Closure confirms acceptance and disbands the temporary project; these teams are still delivering.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The delivery organization has a strong blame culture, and staff hide bad news about delays. Which people factor should be addressed?
questions.why: A blame culture discourages openness; effective leadership should support trust, honest information and safe escalation.
optionWhy: A product hierarchy helps plan outputs, not repair harmful team norms.
Contract terms may matter but do not alone create openness and trust within the project ecosystem.
A blame culture discourages openness; effective leadership should support trust, honest information and safe escalation.
Extra budget does not automatically change behaviours that suppress reporting.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A project includes specialists with the right technical skills but no experience of the chosen delivery method. What should be considered?
options: Replacing all experienced staff with new hires
questions.why: An effective team needs appropriate capabilities and competence; gaps should be understood and addressed.
optionWhy: A blanket replacement is unnecessary when focused development may close the capability gap.
Stakeholder engagement remains necessary and is unrelated to whether staff need training.
Management stages are part of PRINCE2 control and are not removed to address training needs.
An effective team needs appropriate capabilities and competence; gaps should be understood and addressed.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A team works across three time zones. What should influence how it communicates?
options: Working arrangements and accessible communication channels
The fixed physical location of the project board
The total number of outputs in the project plan
questions.why: Communication methods should accommodate remote, hybrid and geographically dispersed contributors.
optionWhy: Communication methods should accommodate remote, hybrid and geographically dispersed contributors.
Communication needs span the project ecosystem and are not set solely by one stakeholder.
The board's meeting location does not determine suitable methods for an international team.
The number of products does not determine whether communication needs to be asynchronous or accessible.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A new trade union representative becomes important because the project affects working patterns. What should the project team do?
options: Remove all existing users from the stakeholder list
Review stakeholder engagement and communication arrangements
Wait until closing a project to communicate
Automatically appoint the representative as executive
questions.why: Relevant stakeholders and their influence can change during the lifecycle, so engagement plans should be reviewed.
optionWhy: New stakeholder involvement supplements rather than invalidates existing stakeholder needs.
Relevant stakeholders and their influence can change during the lifecycle, so engagement plans should be reviewed.
Late engagement risks resistance and missed requirements during the change.
Executive accountability represents business interests and is not automatically transferred to an influencer.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: An external charity can influence whether the intended project benefits are accepted, even without a project role. What is it?
questions.why: A stakeholder may affect, be affected by or consider itself affected by the project; formal appointment is not required.
optionWhy: Project support provides services to the project team, not a label for any outside organization.
A risk action owner is specifically assigned to implement agreed risk actions.
A stakeholder may affect, be affected by or consider itself affected by the project; formal appointment is not required.
A team manager controls delivery of delegated work packages rather than representing every external interest.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A manager sends a detailed report but fails to learn that community groups cannot understand its technical language. What communication improvement is best?
options: Send the same report more often
Delegate the entire communication function to the supplier
Adapt content to the audience and seek feedback
questions.why: Effective communication considers different audiences and verifies that messages are understood.
optionWhy: Increasing frequency does not solve a language or accessibility barrier.
Avoiding communication would worsen stakeholder misunderstanding.
The approach must address the project ecosystem, not just one supplier group.
Effective communication considers different audiences and verifies that messages are understood.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: An organization asks how the project will support adoption after installing a new service. Which concern is central to change management?
options: Helping people transition from current working practices to the target state
Replacing the business case with a work package
questions.why: A new product alone does not ensure people adopt changed routines and realize intended outcomes.
optionWhy: A new product alone does not ensure people adopt changed routines and realize intended outcomes.
Product identification helps change control but does not by itself drive behavioural adoption.
Meeting duration has no direct connection to planning effective transition or adoption.
A work package governs team work and cannot replace justification for the investment.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A temporary team includes people from different professional and cultural backgrounds. What approach is most consistent with the people element?
options: Allow only project board members to propose improvements
Value diverse perspectives and agree effective ways of working together
Assume everyone uses the same communication style
Exclude stakeholders outside the project organization
questions.why: Teams benefit from cultural awareness, inclusion, clarity and trust in cross-functional collaboration.
optionWhy: Continuous improvement and useful feedback can come from people throughout the project ecosystem.
Teams benefit from cultural awareness, inclusion, clarity and trust in cross-functional collaboration.
Differences in working preferences need to be understood, not ignored.
People affected by the project remain relevant even when outside the immediate team.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A new digital service is completed and available to customers. What does its availability represent before anyone changes their behaviour?
questions.why: The service is a deliverable produced by project activity; outcomes arise when people use it differently.
optionWhy: A benefit is a measurable improvement resulting from an outcome, such as reduced waiting times.
A business objective is an organizational goal to which the project contributes, not simply a delivered service.
The service is a deliverable produced by project activity; outcomes arise when people use it differently.
An outcome is the result of changed behaviours or circumstances following use of an output.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: After a new scheduling tool is introduced, staff stop manually allocating appointments. Which term best describes the changed working practice?
questions.why: The changed way staff work is a result of using the product, so it is an outcome.
optionWhy: The tool itself is the output; its effect on everyday practices is an outcome.
A benefit is a measurable improvement such as lower staffing cost or shorter waiting times resulting from the outcome.
A product description specifies what a product should be; it is not the change in staff behaviour.
The changed way staff work is a result of using the product, so it is an outcome.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A new system reduces the average claims-processing time from 12 days to 7 days. What is the five-day reduction?
questions.why: The measurable improvement from the changed service is a benefit attributable to the outcome.
optionWhy: The measurable improvement from the changed service is a benefit attributable to the outcome.
The output is a delivered product or capability, such as the new system.
The improvement is an observed or forecast positive effect, not an uncertain event threatening or helping objectives.

questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A new transport system improves journey times but creates extra noise for nearby residents. How should the expected noise impact be described?
questions.why: A dis-benefit is an anticipated measurable adverse result of an outcome, considered in business justification.
optionWhy: A checkpoint report summarizes team progress at set intervals, not the investment trade-off.

Extra noise is an adverse effect rather than a measurable improvement.
A work package describes work delegated to a team, not unwanted consequences for residents.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A university plans to measure staff time saved by a new admissions system 18 months after project closure. Which management product should assign the ownership and timing of that review?
questions.why: This approach specifies benefit measurement actions, reviews, ownership and timings, including relevant post-project reviews.
optionWhy: An issue report analyses and recommends action for a specific issue, not overall benefit measurement.
A product register tracks product status rather than the achievement of operational benefits.
This approach specifies benefit measurement actions, reviews, ownership and timings, including relevant post-project reviews.
The business case documents justification and expected benefits; it is not the detailed review schedule.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A sustainability performance target must be monitored during delivery. Which management product explains how such targets will be managed?
questions.why: This approach defines management actions and controls for meeting agreed sustainability performance targets.
optionWhy: The quality register records product quality activities; it does not set the overall sustainability management approach.
A checkpoint report gives periodic team progress rather than defining sustainability controls.
The risk register tracks uncertainties, not all sustainability actions and target measurement arrangements.
This approach defines management actions and controls for meeting agreed sustainability performance targets.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Before agreeing substantial investment, the board asks for more detailed costs, benefits, options and risks than were available during start-up. Which product should have been developed further?
questions.why: The outline justification is developed into a fuller business case to support authorization of significant project investment.
optionWhy: The outline justification is developed into a fuller business case to support authorization of significant project investment.
A team plan manages specialist delivery and does not replace investment appraisal.
A daily log records informal events and actions, not the complete investment justification.
A product register identifies and tracks products; it cannot justify the business investment.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: In the business case management technique, a review finds costs have doubled. What is the purpose of checking the justification?
options: To eliminate the need to update forecasts
To determine whether the investment remains worthwhile
To guarantee that all forecast benefits have already occurred
To authorize a team plan without project board control
questions.why: Checking tests continued desirability, viability and achievability in light of current estimates and assumptions.
optionWhy: Checking is precisely when assumptions and forecasts should be questioned and refreshed.
Checking tests continued desirability, viability and achievability in light of current estimates and assumptions.
Benefits can arise after delivery and are not guaranteed by checking the business case.
The business case informs investment decisions; it does not supersede delegated authorization.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which TWO statements are correct about business justification? 1. Expected dis-benefits can affect an investment decision. 2. Project justification is only documented after closure. 3. The executive is accountable for the business case. 4. The team manager owns the business case.
questions.why: Statements 1 and 3 are true: adverse consequences are part of the investment picture and the executive owns business justification.
optionWhy: Both are false: the business case is not deferred until closure and is not owned by the team manager.

questions.stem: A sponsor claims the project must stay open until every benefits target has been fully demonstrated. What is the most accurate correction?
options: The project manager must keep the project open forever
Only suppliers are responsible for realizing business benefits
Benefit forecasts should be discarded as soon as a product is accepted
Some benefits may need to be measured after project closure
questions.why: The benefits management approach can arrange follow-up reviews in operations when benefits take time to appear.

questions.stem: A business needs one person to carry ultimate project accountability and own the business case. Who should fill this role?

questions.stem: A museum needs someone to safeguard the needs of visitors and ensure its new exhibition delivers intended user benefits. Which board role?
questions.why: The senior user represents user needs and the approach to realizing intended benefits.

The senior supplier represents the technical and resource capability needed to create products.

questions.stem: A supplier team is uncertain whether specialist engineers will be available to build a product to specification. Which board interest should ensure that capability?
questions.why: The senior supplier represents delivery expertise, supplier resources and technical integrity.
optionWhy: The executive is ultimately accountable for overall business investment rather than day-to-day supplier capability.

The senior supplier represents delivery expertise, supplier resources and technical integrity.
The senior user defines and represents the needs and benefits of product users.

questions.stem: A parent organization sets the total project cost and time tolerance before the project board starts directing work. Which management layer does this?
questions.why: The commissioning business layer sets overall requirements and project-level tolerance boundaries for the board.

questions.stem: A project board authorizes a stage and delegates the day-to-day control of its delivery. Who receives that authority?

questions.stem: Why must project assurance remain independent from the project manager?
options: Because quality assurance and project assurance are identical

Because project assurance has authority to approve all team plans
Because the project manager must not receive any advice
questions.why: Assurance safeguards business, user and supplier interests without being controlled by the person it is assessing.

questions.stem: A specialist team needs meeting coordination, document tracking and help using the project management tools. Which role typically provides this?
questions.why: Project support provides administrative, coordination and technical support services to project management.
optionWhy: The executive is responsible for business justification and the project's ultimate accountability.

questions.stem: A project manager agrees a work package with a team manager. Who controls the specialists performing that package?
questions.why: The team manager organizes and delivers the agreed work package within the delegated constraints.

questions.stem: A project manager must decide how project work packages map to specialist teams. Which structure is especially useful?

Produce a full detailed project plan for all specialist work
Prepare a plan for the initiation stage
questions.why: Start-up sets out the work required to investigate and establish detailed project foundations.
optionWhy: The board authorizes the project after initiation documents have been prepared and reviewed.
Detailed overall planning is developed during initiation and later detailed stage planning.
The end project report is prepared for closing a project, not before initiation begins.
Start-up sets out the work required to investigate and establish detailed project foundations.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15
