questions.stem: The executive and project manager are identified and lessons from similar efforts reviewed. Which process is being performed?
questions.why: The project management team is initially appointed and previous lessons are considered during start-up.
optionWhy: The project management team is initially appointed and previous lessons are considered during start-up.
Controlling a stage authorizes work and monitors delivery after a stage is authorized.
Closure evaluates success and recommendations near the project's end.
Managing a stage boundary reviews a completed stage and prepares information for the next stage.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The project board has received the request to initiate and now decides whether to authorize initiation. Which process contains that board decision?
questions.why: The project board uses directing a project to authorize initiation, the project, stages and closure.
optionWhy: Managing product delivery governs specialist work packages, not board authorization of initiation.
The project board uses directing a project to authorize initiation, the project, stages and closure.
Starting up a project prepares and submits the initiation request but does not itself grant the board's authorization.
Initiating a project creates the detailed documentation after initiation has been authorized.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which process runs from pre-project decisions through final project closure at the directing management level?
questions.why: The board exercises overall control and takes key decisions across the project lifecycle.
optionWhy: Managing product delivery covers team acceptance, execution and delivery of work packages.
Starting up a project occurs before initiation and does not govern every later decision.
The board exercises overall control and takes key decisions across the project lifecycle.
Controlling a stage covers the project manager's work within a specific management stage.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: The [?] process enables the project board to exercise overall control while delegating day-to-day management.
questions.why: Directing a project is the board-level process through which strategic decisions and authorizations are made.
optionWhy: Controlling a stage is led by the project manager within an authorized management stage.
Initiating a project defines the management baseline so the board can decide whether to proceed.
Managing product delivery governs the project manager/team manager interface.
Directing a project is the board-level process through which strategic decisions and authorizations are made.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: During which process is the detailed business case developed and the project initiation documentation assembled?
questions.why: Initiating a project develops the full justification, approaches and controls used to establish firm project foundations.
optionWhy: Initiating a project develops the full justification, approaches and controls used to establish firm project foundations.
Start-up creates the outline case and project brief, before the detailed initiation work.
Stage boundary work updates existing plans and justifications in light of performance; it does not normally build the initial PID.
Closing a project evaluates actual project performance and prepares handover and follow-on actions.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The business needs to understand precisely how the project will be managed before committing major resources. Which process has that purpose?
questions.why: Initiating a project establishes enough detail about delivery, governance, controls and justification for informed authorization.
optionWhy: Start-up checks whether initiation is worthwhile; it does not create the full management baseline.
Initiating a project establishes enough detail about delivery, governance, controls and justification for informed authorization.
This process governs team-level execution of work packages already authorized.
Closure occurs at the end, not before major authorization to proceed.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A project manager monitors delivered work packages, authorizes new ones and sends highlight reports to the board. Which process?
questions.why: These activities are central to the project manager's control of an authorized management stage.
optionWhy: Starting up a project decides whether there is enough justification to initiate.
A stage boundary reviews the stage and plans the next one rather than controlling everyday work packages.
These activities are central to the project manager's control of an authorized management stage.
The project board uses directing a project to authorize stages and make major decisions.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The project manager learns that a current-stage issue could require corrective action without breaching stage tolerance. Which process permits day-to-day correction?
questions.why: Within delegated authority, the project manager can take corrective action to maintain an authorized stage.
optionWhy: A stage boundary is a planned control point for reviewing completed stages or requested exceptions.
Board direction is required when decisions exceed the project manager's authority, not for every within-tolerance action.
Closure is intended to wind down the project, not resolve ordinary current-stage deviations.
Within delegated authority, the project manager can take corrective action to maintain an authorized stage.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which TWO activities are associated with controlling a stage? 1. Authorize work packages. 2. Approve the next stage plan as project board. 3. Review work package status. 4. Confirm final project closure.
questions.why: Authorizing work packages and reviewing their progress are project manager duties within controlling a stage.
optionWhy: Authorizing work packages and reviewing their progress are project manager duties within controlling a stage.
Statement 2 belongs to the project board's directing decision, not the project manager's controlling a stage process.
Both are board-level decisions within directing a project, not the ongoing stage control activities.
Statement 4 is a board decision about closing the whole project, not a stage-control activity.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The specialist team formally agrees the work it will undertake, creates products and reports progress back. Which process focuses on that agreement?
questions.why: Managing product delivery controls accepting, executing and handing back work agreed in a work package.
optionWhy: Closing a project confirms final acceptance and handover of the overall project.
Managing product delivery controls accepting, executing and handing back work agreed in a work package.
Directing a project is the board's governance process rather than the specialist team's package work.
Stage boundary work prepares reviews and plans for the next authorized stage.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: A team manager uses the [?] process to accept, execute and deliver the work package.
questions.why: The team manager's core delivery interface with the project manager is managing product delivery.
optionWhy: Start-up sets up the possibility of initiation, not execution of authorized delivery work.
Stage boundary work gives the board review and planning information between management stages.
The team manager's core delivery interface with the project manager is managing product delivery.
Directing a project governs project board authorizations, not team work package completion.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A project manager has prepared the end stage report, updated the business case and drafted the next stage plan. Which process is this?
questions.why: At a stage boundary, information is prepared so the board can review performance and authorize the next stage.
optionWhy: That process controls team work packages rather than board stage decisions.
Start-up prepares the first project brief and initiation stage plan before initiation.
Closure reviews the whole project and confirms acceptance, not generally the next management stage.
At a stage boundary, information is prepared so the board can review performance and authorize the next stage.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: The project board requests an exception plan because the existing stage plan is no longer viable. Which process normally prepares the replacement plan?
questions.why: Managing a stage boundary supports preparation and submission of an exception plan after board direction.
optionWhy: Managing a stage boundary supports preparation and submission of an exception plan after board direction.
Team-level delivery cannot independently replace an authorized management-stage baseline.
The board requests and approves an exception plan but does not generally prepare it.
The project has already begun and a stage exception is not part of initial start-up.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: At project completion, the organization needs formal product acceptance, handover and a list of unresolved actions for operations. Which process?
questions.why: Closing a project confirms acceptance, evaluates delivery and ensures follow-on actions are appropriately handed over.
optionWhy: Initiation creates the baseline; it does not confirm whether final delivery met the baseline.
Closing a project confirms acceptance, evaluates delivery and ensures follow-on actions are appropriately handed over.
Start-up precedes initiation and cannot confirm final product acceptance.
Stage control handles current work packages but does not provide the overall closure decision point.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about closing a project are correct? 1. Some benefit reviews may be planned for after closure. 2. Every expected benefit must already be achieved. 3. Final user acceptance should be checked. 4. Only the team manager may authorize final closure.
questions.why: Post-project benefit reviews can be arranged, and user acceptance must be checked before orderly closure.
optionWhy: Both are false: complete benefits realization is not required, and a team manager does not authorize project closure.
Statement 4 is false: the project board authorizes closure, not the team manager.
Post-project benefit reviews can be arranged, and user acceptance must be checked before orderly closure.
Statement 2 is false: benefits can arise during post-project operation, so not all must be achieved by closure.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which is NOT an accountability of the senior supplier on the project board?
options: Ensuring suitable supplier resources are committed
Protecting the technical integrity of specialist products
Owning the business case and the overall investment justification
questions.why: Business case ownership belongs to the executive, who represents the business interest.
optionWhy: The senior supplier represents the supplier community in project governance.
Supplier resource availability and commitment are part of the supplier representative's role.
The senior supplier has responsibility for the technical integrity of supplier-delivered products.
Business case ownership belongs to the executive, who represents the business interest.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT normally a time-driven progress control?
options: Exception report issued following a forecast stage tolerance breach
Scheduled weekly work package progress check
questions.why: An exception report is triggered by an event: the forecast of exceeding tolerance, not by a regular calendar interval.
optionWhy: An exception report is triggered by an event: the forecast of exceeding tolerance, not by a regular calendar interval.
A weekly checkpoint is a time-driven report at a fixed recurring interval.
Monthly highlight reporting is a time-driven project manager-to-board control.
A prearranged weekly review is time-driven because it follows a fixed timetable.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which statement does NOT describe a risk in PRINCE2?
options: An uncertain threat with assessed likelihood and impact
A known off-specification which requires a decision now
An uncertain event that may increase project costs
An uncertain event that may improve benefits
questions.why: An off-specification is an issue because an agreed product requirement is known not to be met.
optionWhy: Identifying probability and impact is consistent with assessing a risk.
An off-specification is an issue because an agreed product requirement is known not to be met.
A possible future cost increase is a negative project risk or threat.
A possible beneficial outcome is an opportunity, which is also a risk.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: Which activity is NOT an objective of starting up a project?
options: Appoint the initial executive and project manager
Establish an outline business case and project brief
Authorize the full delivery project after approving its detailed PID
questions.why: Full project authorization is a board decision in directing a project after the PID has been developed during initiating a project.
optionWhy: Initial appointment of the key leaders occurs during starting up a project.
These start-up products make it possible to decide whether initiating the project is worthwhile.
Full project authorization is a board decision in directing a project after the PID has been developed during initiating a project.
Start-up prepares an initial stage plan for the work needed to initiate the project.
questions.source: Independent Foundation practice, research edition v15

questions.stem: A team asks which integrated PRINCE2 element covers the specific setting in which this project operates. Which one is it?
questions.why: Project context includes organizational and commercial environment, delivery method and other local circumstances.
optionWhy: Processes define the lifecycle activities, not the situation surrounding this project.
Practices address recurring management disciplines, not the project environment itself.
Principles are obligations governing PRINCE2 use, not the particular organizational setting.
Project context includes organizational and commercial environment, delivery method and other local circumstances.

questions.stem: A team releases a usable part of a product, takes feedback, then improves and extends it in repeated cycles. Which delivery approach is described?
questions.why: The team learns and extends the product across successive increments, which is iterative-incremental delivery.
optionWhy: A linear-sequential approach progresses through a mostly defined sequence rather than repeated feedback-led increments.
The team learns and extends the product across successive increments, which is iterative-incremental delivery.
Hybrid combines different delivery approaches; the scenario describes only iterative-incremental work.
Stage-based governance is a PRINCE2 principle, not the delivery approach used to create the product.

questions.stem: Two organizations each replace a payroll system. Why can both still be considered unique projects?
options: They have distinct contexts, people, requirements or constraints
Neither can use an established supplier
Every project must invent a new technology
The projects cannot use comparable plans
questions.why: Even similar undertakings differ in their circumstances, stakeholders or products; uniqueness does not require novelty in every activity.
optionWhy: Even similar undertakings differ in their circumstances, stakeholders or products; uniqueness does not require novelty in every activity.
Using the same supplier is compatible with a unique project and may be useful for learning from experience.
A project can deliver change using proven products and methods without inventing technology.
A similar planning structure may be tailored and reused; the context remains unique.

questions.stem: A regulator imposes additional data-retention rules on a project midway through delivery. Which part of the project context is most directly relevant?
options: The external regulatory and organizational environment
Whether a project has seven principles
questions.why: Regulatory requirements are contextual constraints to consider when tailoring and maintaining project plans.
optionWhy: Management stages are governance boundaries; the new requirement primarily changes the external environment.
Checkpoint frequency is a progress control, not the source of a new regulatory obligation.
Regulatory requirements are contextual constraints to consider when tailoring and maintaining project plans.
PRINCE2 principles remain applicable irrespective of this change in regulatory requirements.

questions.stem: A business case was compelling at authorization but costs now exceed the likely benefits. Which principle requires renewed justification?
questions.why: The project must remain worthwhile, not simply have had a good business case at its start.
optionWhy: This directs attention to the products and their quality rather than deciding whether continued investment is worthwhile.
The project must remain worthwhile, not simply have had a good business case at its start.
Lessons may inform the decision but do not replace the requirement for ongoing business justification.
Stages create decision points; it is the business justification principle that requires ongoing value.

questions.stem: A manager records an unexpected problem and alters the next stage approach after discussing what the team learned. Which principle is shown?
questions.why: Identifying and applying a lesson during the project demonstrates learning rather than filing lessons only at closure.
optionWhy: Exception control concerns delegated authority and forecasts against tolerances, not continuous learning.
A product focus defines the required outputs, but the scenario emphasizes changing future working based on experience.
Identifying and applying a lesson during the project demonstrates learning rather than filing lessons only at closure.
Tailoring adjusts the method to context; this change is specifically based on a captured lesson.

questions.stem: A small internal project has one person fulfilling both project support and team manager duties. Which statement best reflects tailoring?
options: This can be acceptable if responsibilities are clear and role constraints are respected
Every PRINCE2 role must be a different person
The project manager should also provide independent project assurance
The project may omit the business justification principle
questions.why: Some roles can be combined when suitable, but accountability and independence constraints must remain intact.
optionWhy: Some roles can be combined when suitable, but accountability and independence constraints must remain intact.
PRINCE2 permits suitable role combinations; a small team does not automatically require separate individuals for every role.
Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager and cannot simply be absorbed into that role.
All seven principles remain necessary even for a very small project.

questions.stem: The project board approves a stage plan and delegates delivery to the project manager within agreed bounds. Which principle primarily enables this?
questions.why: Tolerances provide boundaries within which lower levels can act without routine escalation.
optionWhy: Learning improves future decisions but does not establish the delegated authority in this scenario.
The plan should be product-focused, but the key is delegated decision rights.
Tailoring affects how procedures and documentation are applied, not the core authority mechanism described.
Tolerances provide boundaries within which lower levels can act without routine escalation.

questions.stem: Which project action most directly demonstrates the focus on products principle?
options: Start by listing team members’ favourite activities
Approve the supplier invoice before stating acceptance criteria
Define the required product and acceptance criteria before estimating tasks
Use the same report template for every stage regardless of need
questions.why: Starting with the result and its quality expectations keeps the project focused on deliverables.
optionWhy: Activity lists may be needed later, but they should flow from clearly defined required products.
Payments do not establish what products must be delivered or how they will be accepted.
Starting with the result and its quality expectations keeps the project focused on deliverables.
Rigid templates are not the essence of product focus and may obstruct appropriate tailoring.

questions.stem: Which action is consistent with tailoring while retaining PRINCE2?
options: Removing the manage by stages principle to save time
Using a concise combined digital management product with the required information
Allowing the project manager to act as their own independent assurance
Omitting approval for a new stage regardless of risk
questions.why: A documented product can be simplified or combined if control, information and accountability needs are satisfied.
optionWhy: Principles are universal and cannot be dropped under the pretext of tailoring.
A documented product can be simplified or combined if control, information and accountability needs are satisfied.
This breaks the independence of project assurance, not a permitted simplification.
Stage boundaries and control remain important; tailoring does not erase PRINCE2 governance.

questions.stem: The team discovers stakeholder responsibilities are unclear. Which principle most clearly addresses this?
questions.why: The principle requires defined accountabilities and effective relationships across the stakeholder interests.
optionWhy: Stages divide management decisions but do not themselves settle who is accountable for each activity.
Past lessons might help clarify responsibilities but are not the defining principle.
The principle requires defined accountabilities and effective relationships across the stakeholder interests.
A business case explains why to invest; it does not substitute for clear role definitions.

questions.stem: A project uses an iterative delivery method but retains board authorizations and clear tolerances. What is this an example of?
options: Replacing PRINCE2 with a software development methodology
Removing the directing a project process
Removing the focus on products principle
questions.why: The method can support different delivery approaches while retaining principles and accountability.
optionWhy: The method can support different delivery approaches while retaining principles and accountability.
An iterative delivery approach can coexist with PRINCE2 rather than replacing its governance.
The board must still make authorization and direction decisions, whatever delivery method is used.
Iterative delivery produces products too; it does not remove the need to define them.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words. A PRINCE2 project is planned, monitored and controlled on a ______ basis.
questions.why: Manage by stages gives the board controlled review and commitment points during the project.
optionWhy: The supplier delivers specialist products, but the governance principle does not describe supplier-only control.
The product register is a useful record; it is not the unit of stage-based management.
Reports may be periodic, but the principle is not tied to monthly scheduling.
Manage by stages gives the board controlled review and commitment points during the project.

questions.stem:
Which two actions demonstrate learning from experience?
1. Seek relevant lessons before initiation.
2. Wait until closure to record any lessons.
3. Update the next stage’s approach based on lessons learned.
4. Use only lessons from this project, never external ones.
questions.why: Both early use of lessons and applying lessons to later stages demonstrate continuous learning.
optionWhy: Seeking past lessons is right, but waiting until closure misses learning and improvement during delivery.
Both early use of lessons and applying lessons to later stages demonstrate continuous learning.
Neither postponing all learning nor refusing outside experience fits the principle.
Applying improvements is right, but lessons from other projects should not be ignored.

questions.stem: A system is delivered, but staff affected by it have not been trained and refuse to adopt it. What does this mainly illustrate?
options: The project should measure only product delivery
People affected by a project matter as well as those delivering it
Every affected person needs a seat on the project board
All benefits are guaranteed by product acceptance
questions.why: Managing change requires attention to the people who must work differently after handover.
optionWhy: The output alone is insufficient to ensure the change is adopted or benefits realized.
Managing change requires attention to the people who must work differently after handover.
Stakeholders must be engaged but need not all be board members.
Acceptance of the product does not guarantee its use or achievement of forecast benefits.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes leadership from management in a project?
options: Leadership is budget control; management is motivating change
Management is unnecessary if leadership is strong
Leadership influences direction and commitment; management coordinates work and controls
Leadership belongs only to the project executive
questions.why: Leadership builds commitment to change while management plans, organizes and monitors delivery.
optionWhy: That reverses the broad distinction: management organizes and controls, while leadership creates direction and motivation.
Effective projects require both effective organization/control and purposeful direction.
Leadership builds commitment to change while management plans, organizes and monitors delivery.
People at different levels can demonstrate leadership, not only the board.

questions.stem: A project has a formal stakeholder list but no two-way conversations with affected teams. What is missing?
questions.why: Engagement involves listening and shaping the change, not just storing stakeholder names.
optionWhy: A plan describes work and control, but it cannot replace meaningful dialogue with those affected.
Product descriptions clarify quality and expectations; they are not a stakeholder engagement process.
An exception report addresses forecast tolerance breaches, not ongoing engagement.
Engagement involves listening and shaping the change, not just storing stakeholder names.

questions.stem: A charity project must send board updates by email, staff demos in person, and patient surveys online. Which PID approach specifies this mix of communication and feedback?
questions.why: It describes communication needs, channels, responsibilities, frequencies and feedback arrangements.
optionWhy: This sets quality standards and responsibilities, not the frequency and channels of stakeholder communication.
It describes communication needs, channels, responsibilities, frequencies and feedback arrangements.
This sets how uncertainties will be identified and handled; it does not govern general stakeholder communications.
A work package formally delegates specified product delivery work, not project-wide stakeholder engagement.

questions.stem: A department must adopt new working practices after a product is delivered. Where should planned activities to support this transition be described?
questions.why: This explains how changes to working practices and their adoption by affected people will be managed.
optionWhy: The product register records product status and information, not the people-focused adoption arrangements.
Lessons may be recorded about adoption, but planned transition actions belong in the change management approach.
This explains how changes to working practices and their adoption by affected people will be managed.
A resistance risk could be recorded there, but it is not the overall transition approach.

questions.stem: A team includes multiple languages and working cultures. Which capability most directly helps leaders collaborate effectively across these differences?
options: An extra management stage in every case
Removing remote workers from the team
questions.why: Understanding and working respectfully across cultural contexts supports effective diverse teams.
optionWhy: Understanding and working respectfully across cultural contexts supports effective diverse teams.
Exception reports concern forecast tolerance breaches, not basic team collaboration.
A stage boundary does not by itself improve cross-cultural relationships.
Eliminating diversity is not a PRINCE2 method for effective team management.

questions.stem: A team member can perform a task but does not have enough available hours for it. Which distinction matters?
questions.why: Capability concerns ability; capacity concerns available resources or time to do the work.
optionWhy: Capability concerns ability; capacity concerns available resources or time to do the work.
These both concern risk and do not explain the team member’s availability.
These concern planning levels, not the availability of qualified staff.
These distinguish delivered products from changes arising from their use, not staffing availability.

questions.stem: A distributed team argues about handover standards and deadlines. Which action best supports effective collaboration?
options: Keep team members apart and avoid discussing differences
Agree working practices, communication norms and interfaces together
Escalate every disagreement to the business layer
questions.why: Shared, explicit working practices and co-creation improve trust and coordination across locations.
optionWhy: Avoiding clarification leaves conflicting expectations and weakens trust.
Shared, explicit working practices and co-creation improve trust and coordination across locations.
The business layer does not manage every day-to-day working disagreement.
Quality criteria specify what the product must achieve; removing them is not a collaboration remedy.

questions.stem: A senior stakeholder announces a change without explaining why it matters to staff. Which leadership improvement is most relevant?
options: Increase the number of checkpoint reports
Replace the issue register with a spreadsheet
Explain the vision and involve affected people in the change
Ask project assurance to approve every team conversation
questions.why: Leadership helps people understand and support a future state rather than merely receive instructions.
optionWhy: Checkpoint reports track delegated delivery work, not the purpose people see in the change.
The recording format does not create commitment or understanding.
Leadership helps people understand and support a future state rather than merely receive instructions.
Assurance provides independent review, not approval of all dialogue.

questions.stem: Why is the change management approach relevant even when specialist products are technically complete?
options: It eliminates the need for user acceptance
It ensures all financial benefits arise instantly
It supports adoption of the new state and achievement of outcomes
questions.why: Delivered outputs create value only if people and operations use them to achieve intended change.
optionWhy: Technical products still need to satisfy requirements and appropriate acceptance.
Benefits may be realized long after the project closes and are not guaranteed by a document.
Business justification remains necessary regardless of how transition is planned.
Delivered outputs create value only if people and operations use them to achieve intended change.

questions.stem:
Which two practices make communication with stakeholders effective?
1. Match channels and frequency to stakeholder needs.
2. Send every stakeholder exactly the same technical detail.
3. Seek feedback and respond to it.
4. Restrict engagement to members of the project management team.
questions.why: Both appropriate communication design and two-way feedback support engagement and collaboration.
optionWhy: Matching needs is useful, but identical detail for every stakeholder ignores different interests and capabilities.
Uniform technical messages and exclusion of affected stakeholders would weaken engagement.
Both appropriate communication design and two-way feedback support engagement and collaboration.
Feedback helps, but stakeholders affected by the change may sit outside the project team.

questions.stem: Who may need to be engaged when project products change operational job roles?
options: Only the team members building the product
People working on the project and those affected by its change
questions.why: PRINCE2’s people element covers both the project ecosystem and stakeholders impacted by its outcomes.
optionWhy: The project manager coordinates work but is not the only person affected by operational changes.
Suppliers represent delivery needs; users and operational staff may be the most affected.
Building the product does not capture the needs of all people who must use or support it.
PRINCE2’s people element covers both the project ecosystem and stakeholders impacted by its outcomes.

questions.stem: A team member has technical expertise but repeatedly ignores agreed working practices. Which is the most complete way to view team effectiveness?
options: Consider skills, behaviours, relationships and working culture together
Ignore relationships as outside the project
Replace all team collaboration with formal reports
questions.why: Team effectiveness depends on more than specialist skill, including collaboration and the ability to work together.
optionWhy: Team effectiveness depends on more than specialist skill, including collaboration and the ability to work together.
Technical skill does not guarantee the required collaboration, behaviour or relationships.
Relationships are part of the people element and influence the success of change.
Formal reports do not remove the need for cooperative working and feedback.

questions.stem: A user group is influential but skeptical about a proposed new process. What is the best initial response?
options: Understand their concerns and involve them in shaping the change
Treat skepticism as proof of an exception situation
Ignore them because they are not on the project board
Record the group only in the risk register and stop communicating
questions.why: Engagement should be two-way and responsive to affected people’s motivations and needs.
optionWhy: Engagement should be two-way and responsive to affected people’s motivations and needs.
An exception is a forecast tolerance breach; concern from stakeholders does not automatically create one.
Stakeholders can affect project success even without formal board roles.
Resistance may create risks, but a risk register alone is not a stakeholder engagement strategy.

questions.stem: Identify the missing word. The ______ management approach in the PID describes how feedback is gathered and information shared with stakeholders.
questions.why: The communication management approach defines who needs information, how it will be communicated and when.
optionWhy: The benefits management approach addresses benefit reviews and realization, not general communication arrangements.
The commercial management approach addresses commercial relationships and supplier arrangements.
The communication management approach defines who needs information, how it will be communicated and when.
The quality management approach focuses on verifying product quality against requirements.

questions.stem:
Project staff understand what to build but do not know how the organization will change after delivery. Which two actions help most?
1. Describe the current and target operating states.
2. Treat organizational adoption as outside project concerns.
3. Plan transition and communication with affected users.
4. Measure project success only by completion of technical work.
questions.why: A clear desired future state and planned transition/engagement help people make the change.
optionWhy: Understanding the transition is useful, but dismissing adoption contradicts the people element.
A clear desired future state and planned transition/engagement help people make the change.
Ignoring adoption and measuring only outputs overlooks whether outcomes and benefits occur.
Transition planning helps, but technical completion alone is not sufficient to show change success.

questions.stem: A team has specialists with strong individual skills but poor cooperation. What is the most likely gap?
options: Team cohesion and effective working relationships
questions.why: Individual skills alone do not create trust, shared goals or coordinated delivery.
optionWhy: A product register is useful, but the description concerns how people work together.
Individual skills alone do not create trust, shared goals or coordinated delivery.
Tolerance limits define authority; they do not themselves create collaborative working.
The business case is about investment justification, not the direct team behaviour gap.

questions.stem: A new booking system is delivered to a hospital. Patients then book appointments online. Which is the outcome?
options: A measured reduction of 20 minutes per call
questions.why: An outcome is the change in real-world behaviour following use of the delivered outputs.
optionWhy: The system itself is an output; it does not describe the resulting change in behaviour.
An outcome is the change in real-world behaviour following use of the delivered outputs.
The quantified improvement is a benefit resulting from the changed behaviour.
This management product defines the required project product and its acceptance, not the outcome.

questions.stem: A project replaces travel with video meetings, reducing costs but also reducing local café revenue. What is the café revenue reduction from the investing organization’s perspective if recognized as an expected negative effect?
questions.why: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline from an outcome, perceived as negative by the investing organization.
optionWhy: An output is a product delivered by the project, not a negative measurable consequence.
A benefit is a measurable improvement valued by the investing organization, not a decline perceived as negative.
This is a management record, not the name of an expected measurable decline.
A dis-benefit is a measurable decline from an outcome, perceived as negative by the investing organization.

questions.stem: A project is likely to finish on time but planned operational savings may only arrive two years later. Which approach identifies how the savings will be reviewed after closure?
questions.why: This defines benefit reviews, responsible parties and management actions for realizing benefits, including post-project reviews.
optionWhy: This defines benefit reviews, responsible parties and management actions for realizing benefits, including post-project reviews.
A checkpoint report provides progress on a work package, not a plan for long-term benefit reviews.
The project product description sets the whole project product’s quality and acceptance criteria, not benefits review scheduling.
This escalates forecast tolerance breaches rather than scheduling routine realization measurements.

questions.stem: Which PID approach defines how sustainability targets will be reviewed and controlled?
questions.why: It identifies actions, reviews and controls to meet agreed sustainability performance targets.
optionWhy: Commercial management addresses contractual and supplier relationships, not the primary sustainability controls.
Communication arrangements can report sustainability information but do not themselves define its performance controls.
It identifies actions, reviews and controls to meet agreed sustainability performance targets.
A sustainability-related uncertainty may be recorded as a risk, but this is not the sustainability approach.

questions.stem: At a stage boundary the business case is updated using actual expenditure and revised benefits. What is the main reason?
options: To support a fresh decision on continued investment
To prove all forecast benefits have already been realized
To authorize the team manager to approve the entire project
questions.why: The board needs current cost, risk and benefit forecasts rather than relying solely on assumptions made at initiation.
optionWhy: The board needs current cost, risk and benefit forecasts rather than relying solely on assumptions made at initiation.
Benefits may occur after closure; a stage boundary does not automatically prove their realization.
The business case justifies investment and does not replace product-level definitions.
Project authorization is a directing-level decision, not an automatic result of updating the business case.

questions.stem: Identify the missing word. In the business case technique, ______ means keeping the business case current with actual and forecast information.
questions.why: Maintain keeps the business case updated as the project progresses and information changes.
optionWhy: Confirm relates to checking achieved benefits, not generally updating the case during delivery.
Maintain keeps the business case updated as the project progresses and information changes.
Develop establishes the case and the information used for investment decisions.
Check tests whether justification remains valid; maintenance changes the current case.

questions.stem: Which activity is closest to the CHECK step of business case management?
options: Assess whether remaining cost and risk are justified by expected value
questions.why: Checking the business case tests whether further investment remains desirable, viable and achievable.
optionWhy: Time recording may inform planning but does not itself check continuing business justification.
Product descriptions define deliverables and quality, not directly the desirability of investment.
This supports risk control, not checking the overall case for continued investment.
Checking the business case tests whether further investment remains desirable, viable and achievable.

questions.stem: A project product will be delivered successfully, but the proposed outcome no longer supports the organization’s strategy. What should be revisited?
options: Business case alignment with business objectives
Only the team members’ work instructions
questions.why: Investment needs to remain justified by expected benefits and their contribution to business objectives.
optionWhy: Reporting frequency will not repair a loss of strategic justification.
Successful quality activities do not prove that the outcome is still strategically valuable.
Investment needs to remain justified by expected benefits and their contribution to business objectives.
Work instructions do not resolve whether the project remains worthwhile.

questions.stem:
Which two statements about outputs, outcomes and benefits are CORRECT?
1. A specialist deliverable can be an output.
2. Every output automatically guarantees a benefit.
3. Changed operational behaviour can be an outcome.
4. Benefits can never be measured after closure.
questions.why: Outputs are what gets delivered; outcomes are changes that arise when outputs are used.
optionWhy: A specialist deliverable is an output, but benefits are not guaranteed just by producing it.
Outputs do not guarantee benefits, and many benefits are reviewed after closure.
Outputs are what gets delivered; outcomes are changes that arise when outputs are used.
Changed behaviour is an outcome, but benefits can be measured after the project has ended.

questions.stem: During pre-project work, a small amount of justification is assembled before full initiation. Which management product best captures this initial rationale and scope?
questions.why: The project brief gives a common starting point and can include the outline business case before detailed initiation.
optionWhy: The project brief gives a common starting point and can include the outline business case before detailed initiation.
An end project report evaluates completed project performance rather than setting up the initial case.
This tracks delivery progress on a work package, which has not yet been authorized.
Lessons may be consulted, but the lessons report does not establish the outline case and starting scope.

questions.stem: A project’s senior user requests a feature while the senior supplier worries about technical feasibility. What are these roles representing?
options: User need and supplier delivery capability respectively
The board and the project manager respectively
Quality assurance and project assurance respectively
questions.why: Senior users represent requirements and benefits; senior suppliers represent resources and technical feasibility.
optionWhy: The business viewpoint is represented by the executive; user and supplier interests have different concerns.
Senior users represent requirements and benefits; senior suppliers represent resources and technical feasibility.
Both senior user and senior supplier normally sit on the project board and are not the project manager.
These are assurance concepts, not the three project interests represented by the board.

questions.stem: The project needs to define contracts, procurement relationships and how suppliers will be managed commercially. Which PID product is most relevant?
questions.why: This records how commercial relationships, agreements and supplier arrangements are managed.
optionWhy: Lessons can inform procurement decisions but do not establish the project’s commercial arrangements.
This plans outcomes and benefit realization, not the contractual arrangements.
This records how commercial relationships, agreements and supplier arrangements are managed.
The quality register records quality checks and their results, rather than commercial governance.

questions.stem: A product depends on two specialist teams. Which organizing aid best breaks the delivery work into manageable work elements?
questions.why: A work breakdown structure decomposes the work needed to deliver products and helps organize responsibilities.
optionWhy: A work breakdown structure decomposes the work needed to deliver products and helps organize responsibilities.
The risk register records uncertain threats and opportunities, not a breakdown of activities or work.
This summarizes project performance at completion, not planned work division.
This reports a forecast breach of tolerance, not routine breakdown of delivery work.

questions.stem: Which role remains ultimately accountable for the project’s business case and success?
questions.why: The executive is the single point of accountability and owns the project’s business justification.
optionWhy: Project support supplies administrative and specialist support but is not the overall accountable owner.
The senior supplier represents delivery capability and technical integrity, not overall business accountability.
The project manager manages day-to-day work under board direction; overall accountability lies above that role.
The executive is the single point of accountability and owns the project’s business justification.

questions.stem: A supplier cannot provide the specialist test staff promised for the project. Which project board role should address supplier capacity?
questions.why: The senior supplier is responsible for representing and securing supplier resources and technical capability.
optionWhy: The senior user represents user requirements and benefits, rather than securing supplier expertise.
The senior supplier is responsible for representing and securing supplier resources and technical capability.
Project support may assist administration but is not the board representative for supplier capability.
The executive owns overall justification but specialist supplier commitment is the senior supplier’s focus.

questions.stem: A project manager has sufficient specialist knowledge and wants to manage a small team directly. Which role may they also undertake?
questions.why: The project manager can perform team-manager responsibilities where scale, skills and capacity make this suitable.
optionWhy: The executive is a separate governing role and must not be combined with project manager.
Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager.
The project manager can perform team-manager responsibilities where scale, skills and capacity make this suitable.
The senior user is a board role representing users and is not combined with the project manager.

questions.stem: Which PID product makes clear who has authority and responsibilities in the project management team?
options: Project management team structure and role descriptions
questions.why: The structure and role descriptions show the roles, responsibilities and reporting relationships.
optionWhy: The risk register records individual risks and risk owners, not the entire management structure.
The quality register records planned and completed quality activities, not all governance roles.
This records products and their status, not the decision rights of the project management team.
The structure and role descriptions show the roles, responsibilities and reporting relationships.

questions.stem: The project board has delegated authority to approve certain changes to a named person. Which role has been established?
questions.why: A change authority decides specified requests within limits delegated by the project board.
optionWhy: A change authority decides specified requests within limits delegated by the project board.
A risk action owner carries out a particular response action; they do not receive general change approval rights.
A quality reviewer checks products against criteria but does not automatically authorize changes to baselines.
Assurance independently checks governance and quality but is not synonymous with delegated change approval.

questions.stem: Which step is most relevant when a project reviews who its affected external parties are before designing governance?
questions.why: The organizing technique begins by considering the relevant business, user, supplier and wider relationships.
optionWhy: The end project report is produced near closure, not while designing the initial organizational ecosystem.
The organizing technique begins by considering the relevant business, user, supplier and wider relationships.
A team plan addresses the detailed work of a delivery team, not the broad stakeholder ecosystem.
Quality inspections do not map the full organizational relationships around the project.

questions.stem: The project board wants independent checks but asks the project manager to provide their own assurance. Why is this inappropriate?
options: The project manager is too busy to write reports
All assurance must be done by an external certification body
Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager
Assurance is only needed after closure
questions.why: The board retains accountability for assurance and must maintain an independent line of review.
optionWhy: Workload alone is not the governance reason; independence is the fundamental requirement.
Project assurance can be delegated within the project team if independent of the project manager.
The board retains accountability for assurance and must maintain an independent line of review.
Assurance supports the board during project delivery, not just at the end.

questions.stem: A plan shows that testing cannot start until configuration is complete. What planning concept is described?
questions.why: A dependency is a relationship in which one work item or product relies on another.
optionWhy: Sustainability targets concern environmental or social performance, not the order of activities.
A risk budget funds responses to uncertainty, not the logical relationship between tasks.
A quality specification defines measurable quality requirements, not task sequencing.
A dependency is a relationship in which one work item or product relies on another.

questions.stem: Which management product formally tells a delivery team which products to create and the applicable constraints?
questions.why: It describes the delegated delivery, products, constraints, reporting and acceptance requirements.
optionWhy: The project brief captures the initial project definition before initiation; it does not allocate specific delivery work.
It describes the delegated delivery, products, constraints, reporting and acceptance requirements.
An end stage report evaluates completed stage performance for the board.
An exception report escalates a forecast tolerance breach rather than authorizing ordinary work.

questions.stem: A project is planned in detail for the next stage but only in outline for much later stages. Which concept supports this?
questions.why: Planning detail should reflect the available certainty; near work can be planned more precisely.
optionWhy: The daily log records informal issues and day-to-day notes; it does not govern future planning detail.
Assurance reviews governance but does not define the planning horizon principle.
Planning detail should reflect the available certainty; near work can be planned more precisely.
Exception management responds to forecast tolerance breaches rather than governing planning detail by horizon.

questions.stem: Which statement distinguishes a project plan from a stage plan?
options: The project plan gives the high-level overall picture; a stage plan gives detailed control for one stage
A stage plan replaces the project plan for the whole project
Only the team manager uses a project plan
A project plan is always produced after the final stage
questions.why: The plans serve different management levels and planning horizons.
optionWhy: The plans serve different management levels and planning horizons.
The project plan remains the overall baseline; a stage plan covers a management stage.
The project board uses the project plan for overall monitoring, while the project manager controls stages.
The project plan is assembled during initiation and updated throughout the project.

questions.stem: An approved stage plan can no longer deliver within tolerance. The board asks for a replacement plan. What type is prepared?
questions.why: An approved exception plan replaces the stage or project plan for the period it covers.
optionWhy: A team plan governs delivery of a team’s work package, not the replacement of a breached stage plan.
This defines how benefits will be realized and measured, not the revised stage control plan.
The project brief captures initial scope and justification, not exception recovery plans.
An approved exception plan replaces the stage or project plan for the period it covers.

questions.stem: A project manager starts planning by defining deliverables before listing activities. Which technique does this illustrate?
questions.why: Defining and analysing products first is central to PRINCE2 planning.
optionWhy: Defining and analysing products first is central to PRINCE2 planning.
Risk exposure measures potential effects of uncertainty rather than identifying required products.
Exception management concerns forecasts against tolerances, not the initial product-led planning method.
Quality control tests products against criteria; it is not the technique for creating the plan.

questions.stem: In the PRINCE2 planning technique, which activity should follow defining and analysing products?
questions.why: The planning technique organizes the work packages after clarifying the required products.
optionWhy: Closure occurs after delivery and acceptance, not immediately after identifying products.
A change budget may be part of project controls but is not the immediate next planning activity.
The planning technique organizes the work packages after clarifying the required products.
An exception report is triggered by a forecast breach, not a normal planning step.

questions.stem: Which product primarily defines the full project’s acceptance criteria, rather than one component’s quality checks?
questions.why: This defines what the whole project must deliver, including user quality expectations and acceptance criteria.
optionWhy: This defines what the whole project must deliver, including user quality expectations and acceptance criteria.
The quality register tracks quality activities and results, not overall project product acceptance criteria.
This reports work-package progress, not definition of the full project’s product.
This specifies risk procedures and responsibilities, not acceptance criteria.

questions.stem: A team manager wants to coordinate detailed specialist work within an agreed work package. Which plan is most directly useful, if required?
questions.why: A team plan can organize and control a delivery team’s work under an agreed work package.
optionWhy: The project plan is high-level and covers the whole project rather than daily specialist task organization.
The stage plan supports the project manager’s stage control, not necessarily the team’s detailed task allocation.
An exception plan is prepared when an approved plan needs replacing after a forecast breach.
A team plan can organize and control a delivery team’s work under an agreed work package.

questions.stem:
Which two statements about management stages are correct?
1. They establish control and investment decision points.
2. They must always end at the same time as technical phases.
3. The initiation stage is a management stage.
4. Management stages should overlap to save time.
questions.why: Management stages create decision points, and initiation is the first management stage.
optionWhy: Stage boundaries are governance points, but technical activities need not align exactly with management stages.
Management stages create decision points, and initiation is the first management stage.
Technical and management stages need not coincide, and management stages do not overlap.
Initiation is a management stage, but overlapping management stages is not PRINCE2 stage governance.

questions.stem: A product must process 500 payments per minute during acceptance testing. What type of information is that?
questions.why: A measurable throughput threshold defines a specific characteristic to be verified during quality control.
optionWhy: A broad expectation might be fast processing, but the measurable threshold is a specific quality specification.
A measurable throughput threshold defines a specific characteristic to be verified during quality control.
The business case may expect efficiencies, but a technical throughput limit is a product quality measure.
Risk tolerance is the permitted level of exposure or deviation for a risk objective, not payment throughput.

questions.stem: A test was completed and a product failed against its defined criteria. Which record should reflect the test result?
questions.why: The quality register tracks planned and completed quality activities and their results, including failures.
optionWhy: This tracks uncertain threats and opportunities, not the required history of completed quality activities.
The plan schedules work but is not the detailed record of each quality check and result.
The quality register tracks planned and completed quality activities and their results, including failures.
This tracks how benefits will be realized and reviewed, not specific product test outcomes.

questions.stem: A project manager wants a current list of project products and their status. Which management product is most directly relevant?
questions.why: The product register records the products being managed and their status.
optionWhy: The product register records the products being managed and their status.
The approach defines quality standards and responsibilities, not the live list of product statuses.
This defines how issues and changes are handled, rather than listing the status of products.
An exception report escalates a forecast tolerance breach and is not a product-status list.

questions.stem: A user says a new application must be easy to navigate. Which further step makes the expectation useful for quality control?
options: Assume any screen layout is acceptable
Record it only as a financial risk
Delay defining any quality checks until closure
Agree observable, measurable quality specifications and methods
questions.why: Clear specifications and tests enable the team to check whether the expectation is met.
optionWhy: A vague expectation cannot be reliably tested without clear agreed measures.
Risk assessment is not a substitute for translating a user expectation into quality measures.
Quality expectations need to guide development and checks during delivery.
Clear specifications and tests enable the team to check whether the expectation is met.

questions.stem: What BEST distinguishes quality assurance from product quality control?
options: Assurance always tests every finished product, while control audits the organization
Assurance checks confidence in the quality system; control tests products against specifications
They are two names for the same activity
Control only starts once the project closes
questions.why: Quality assurance is often independently managed, while quality control checks product conformity.
optionWhy: That reverses the emphasis: control checks products; assurance provides confidence in arrangements.
Quality assurance is often independently managed, while quality control checks product conformity.
Their roles differ, even though both contribute to confidence in quality.
Quality-control activities are planned and performed during product development and delivery.

questions.stem: Which management product explains the standards, quality methods and roles to use throughout the project?
questions.why: This defines methods, standards and responsibilities for quality specifications and acceptance criteria.
optionWhy: Checkpoint reporting gives delivery progress, not project-wide rules for managing quality.
The product register records products and statuses, not overall quality procedures.
This defines methods, standards and responsibilities for quality specifications and acceptance criteria.
An issue report analyzes an issue requiring formal consideration, not the general quality process.

questions.stem: A supplier has completed technical testing but the user has not agreed the product meets operational needs. What should the project avoid assuming?
options: That passing technical tests automatically proves user acceptance
That quality testing needs recorded evidence
That quality management runs throughout delivery
questions.why: Technical conformance is not the same as satisfying the user’s agreed acceptance criteria.
optionWhy: Technical conformance is not the same as satisfying the user’s agreed acceptance criteria.
Quality evidence should be recorded and may be linked from the quality register.
Product descriptions do define measurable product requirements and quality criteria.
Quality must be planned and checked as products are created, not only at closure.

questions.stem: Which part of quality management starts by defining what the product must meet and how that will be checked?
questions.why: Quality planning captures specifications and develops product descriptions and the quality approach.
optionWhy: Issue control handles events and baseline changes rather than initially defining quality specifications.
Closure verifies acceptance and handover, but quality expectations are set earlier.
Quality planning captures specifications and develops product descriptions and the quality approach.
An exception report is needed for a forecast tolerance breach, not ordinary quality definition.

questions.stem:
Which two statements about a Product Description are correct?
1. It includes quality criteria for that product.
2. It replaces the project-wide business case.
3. It can specify the quality method to use.
4. It is always the record of completed quality test results.
questions.why: A Product Description states the product’s quality criteria and how those criteria are to be checked.
optionWhy: A Product Description states the product’s quality criteria and how those criteria are to be checked.
Quality criteria belong in a Product Description, but actual check results go in quality records such as the quality register.
Quality methods can be described, but a Product Description does not replace the business case.
The Product Description is neither investment justification nor the running register of completed quality checks.

questions.stem: A project is creating many similar outputs. Which practice helps ensure each product is checked using agreed standards before acceptance?
questions.why: The quality practice defines and applies methods to establish whether products satisfy agreed specifications.
optionWhy: Progress monitors achievements versus plans; it does not by itself set product test methods.
The business case justifies the investment but does not detail every product’s acceptance tests.
Organization allocates accountability but does not alone establish product-checking methods.
The quality practice defines and applies methods to establish whether products satisfy agreed specifications.

questions.stem: A contractor may miss a delivery date because its factory is at risk of flooding. Which phrase describes the risk cause?
options: An exception report to the board
questions.why: The underlying situation creates the possibility of a later risk event.
optionWhy: That is a potential effect on objectives, not the situation giving rise to the uncertainty.
The underlying situation creates the possibility of a later risk event.
That describes the uncertain event which might occur, rather than its underlying cause.
A management product is not the source of the risk.

questions.stem: For a threat, which description best captures risk impact?
options: How likely the event is to occur
How near the event is in time
How rapidly consequences develop after it occurs
The estimated effect on project objectives if it occurs
questions.why: Impact is the magnitude and nature of consequences for project objectives.
optionWhy: Likelihood is probability, not the consequence on objectives.
Proximity describes when an event might occur.
Velocity addresses speed of impact, not size of consequence.
Impact is the magnitude and nature of consequences for project objectives.

questions.stem: A manager estimates the probability of a cyberattack, then considers all identified threats together. Which activity is most relevant to the combined picture?
options: Assessing overall risk exposure or the risk profile
questions.why: Aggregate analysis helps understand the combined effect of risks rather than one risk alone.
optionWhy: An issue concerns something requiring current project management consideration, not combined future uncertainty.
Product definition clarifies outputs, but the question asks for the combined risk picture.
Aggregate analysis helps understand the combined effect of risks rather than one risk alone.
An exception plan responds to an authorized forecast breach rather than describing aggregate risk.

questions.stem: A potential threat is eliminated by selecting a different supplier that has no exposure to the relevant hazard. Which threat response is this?
questions.why: Avoid removes the threat by changing the circumstances that created it or removing the exposure.
optionWhy: Avoid removes the threat by changing the circumstances that created it or removing the exposure.
Reduce lowers probability or impact but does not necessarily remove the threat entirely.
Share involves distributing exposure among parties, not eliminating the source.
Accept recognizes a threat without active mitigation, which is not what switching suppliers achieves.

questions.stem: A favourable uncertainty could be made more likely by funding a small prototype. Which opportunity response is described?
questions.why: Enhance takes action to improve the probability or impact of a potential opportunity.
optionWhy: Avoid is a threat response removing exposure; it would not make an opportunity more likely.
Transfer assigns elements of a threat’s financial impact to another party, not increases opportunity probability.
Enhance takes action to improve the probability or impact of a potential opportunity.
Issue decisions concern current events or proposed changes, not proactively improving an opportunity.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for ensuring that an assigned risk is managed and appropriate responses are monitored?
questions.why: The risk owner is accountable for the assigned risk and for coordinating/monitoring responses.
optionWhy: The risk action owner implements particular responses, but is not necessarily accountable for overall management of the risk.
The risk owner is accountable for the assigned risk and for coordinating/monitoring responses.
Project support may administer the register but is not automatically the owner of every risk.
A quality reviewer tests product conformity; this role does not own a risk by default.

questions.stem: A team notices it is choosing optimistic estimates because it wants the project approved. What should the team address?
questions.why: Recognizing and challenging optimism bias improves the quality of risk assessments and decisions.
optionWhy: More reporting does not necessarily correct biased assessment of uncertainty.
Contracts may affect risks, but the scenario is about decision bias.
Product records are not the cause of systematic optimistic judgments.
Recognizing and challenging optimism bias improves the quality of risk assessments and decisions.

questions.stem: Identify the missing word. The PRINCE2 risk technique includes identify, assess, plan, implement and ______.
questions.why: Risk information needs to be communicated throughout the risk management technique to relevant parties.
optionWhy: Authorization is a governance action, not the fifth named activity in the risk management technique.
Project closure is a separate process, not the name of the ongoing risk communication activity.
Baseline control concerns approved versions of management products and changes to them.
Risk information needs to be communicated throughout the risk management technique to relevant parties.

questions.stem: A project has a high appetite for taking an opportunity, but a defined tolerance threshold for its risk exposure. What is the distinction?
options: Appetite is willingness to take risk; tolerance is a measurable allowed limit
Appetite is a cash reserve; tolerance is a supplier invoice
Both always describe the same money amount
Tolerance tells when a risk might occur
questions.why: Appetite expresses attitude to risk; tolerance sets a measurable boundary for acceptable exposure or performance.
optionWhy: Appetite expresses attitude to risk; tolerance sets a measurable boundary for acceptable exposure or performance.
A cash reserve is a risk budget, not risk appetite.
Appetite and tolerance can be related but have different meanings and may use different measurements.
That describes risk proximity, rather than risk tolerance.

questions.stem: A planned response would lower the financial effect of a threat if it occurs by purchasing insurance. What response does this most closely represent?
questions.why: An insurance agreement transfers specified financial consequences of a threat to another party.
optionWhy: Exploit takes advantage of a positive opportunity and is not a response to insurable financial threat.
An insurance agreement transfers specified financial consequences of a threat to another party.
Enhance increases the probability or positive impact of an opportunity, not a threat.
Insurance is an active response with a cost; accepting alone would not transfer consequences.

questions.stem: A completed product is found to be below its approved specification. Which type of issue is most relevant?
questions.why: A product that will not meet its agreed specification is an off-specification issue.
optionWhy: A business opportunity is an unanticipated positive possibility, not nonconformance with a product baseline.
A product that will not meet its agreed specification is an off-specification issue.
A cause gives rise to a potential future uncertainty; the quality failure has already occurred.
Appetite describes willingness to accept risk, not a defective product.

questions.stem: An employee proposes adding a new report to a signed-off product. What is this proposal?
questions.why: A proposal to alter an already approved baseline is a request for change.
optionWhy: A baseline is the current approved version of controlled products; the proposal is to modify it.
A checkpoint report is periodic team progress information, not a proposed change.
Risk impact refers to effects of an uncertain event, not a deliberate baseline modification proposal.
A proposal to alter an already approved baseline is a request for change.

questions.stem: What should the team check FIRST when assessing a change proposal that may affect scope and benefits?
options: Its effect on the business case, baseline and related objectives
Whether an invoice has already been issued
How to hide the request from stakeholders
Whether all requested changes must automatically be accepted
questions.why: Assessment should consider impacts on project justification, products, time, cost and risks before approval.
optionWhy: Assessment should consider impacts on project justification, products, time, cost and risks before approval.
Invoice status alone is not an adequate assessment of wider project consequences.
Issues should be captured and considered transparently rather than concealed.
A change must be assessed and approved within delegated authority, not accepted automatically.

questions.stem: Which step of the issues technique makes a reasoned comparison of possible responses before an approval decision?
questions.why: The recommend step evaluates possible options and proposes an appropriate response to the decision-maker.
optionWhy: Capturing identifies and records an issue; it does not select a preferred option after analysis.
The recommend step evaluates possible options and proposes an appropriate response to the decision-maker.
Implementation follows the authorization of the selected response.
Closing a project is a distinct lifecycle process, not an issues technique step.

questions.stem: A change has been approved and the controlled product record must be updated. Which step of issue management is this?
questions.why: Implementation carries out the approved action and updates affected baselines and records.
optionWhy: Assess determines likely impacts before a change decision; the change has already been approved.
Recommend compares options and advises the decision-maker before authorization.
Capture logs the issue and establishes its type and priority, usually before assessment.
Implementation carries out the approved action and updates affected baselines and records.

questions.stem: Which management product provides detailed analysis and recommendations for an issue requiring formal handling?
questions.why: An issue report can document description, impact assessment, options and recommendations for a significant issue.
optionWhy: This establishes general risk procedures, not analysis of a particular present issue.
This specifies a product’s components and quality criteria, not the full formal issue analysis.
An issue report can document description, impact assessment, options and recommendations for a significant issue.
A lessons report communicates learning, not approval recommendations for a current formal issue.

questions.stem: A project board delegates approval of small requests for change but retains expensive decisions. What is being tailored?
options: The levels of change authority and delegated limits
The existence of the business justification principle
The requirement to log formal issues
The need to consider product baselines
questions.why: Decision rights may be delegated proportionately, with larger impacts reserved for the board.
optionWhy: Decision rights may be delegated proportionately, with larger impacts reserved for the board.
Delegation cannot remove the requirement for continued business justification.
Delegation does not remove appropriate records and change control for formal issues.
Approved baselines still require controlled amendments irrespective of who authorizes them.

questions.stem: What is the key risk of delegating change approvals too widely without suitable controls?
options: Every request will have to go to the project board
Decisions may drift away from the overall business justification
All changes become future risks instead of issues
Product descriptions can no longer be created
questions.why: Fragmented approvals can weaken alignment between individual changes and the project business case.
optionWhy: Too little delegation causes excessive escalation, not too much delegation.
Fragmented approvals can weaken alignment between individual changes and the project business case.
Requests for change remain issues; the concern is inconsistent authority and alignment.
Product descriptions can still be created, but uncontrolled changes undermine baseline governance.

questions.stem: The team needs project-wide guidance on how requests for change will be captured, assessed, decided and implemented. Where is this found?
questions.why: This defines issue resolution and change-control procedures, responsibilities and delegated authority.
optionWhy: This evaluates performance at closure, not the procedures for managing current changes.
The risk register lists uncertainties and responses, not issue control procedures.
This defines issue resolution and change-control procedures, responsibilities and delegated authority.
The quality register tracks quality checks and results rather than change approval rules.

questions.stem:
Which two statements about issues are correct?
1. An issue can be a concern requiring assessment.
2. Every issue is necessarily a request for change.
3. An unexpected business opportunity may be recorded as an issue.
4. Issues only exist after project closure.
questions.why: Issues include concerns and business opportunities that require project management consideration.
optionWhy: Concerns can be issues, but there are several issue types besides requests for change.
Issues include concerns and business opportunities that require project management consideration.
Issues are not all change requests and can arise at any point during the project.
