Unexpected opportunities can be issues, but issues are managed throughout project delivery.

questions.stem: At a fixed weekly interval, a team manager informs the project manager about work-package delivery. Which report is used?
questions.why: A checkpoint report is the agreed regular team-to-project-manager progress report for a work package.
optionWhy: A highlight report is normally from the project manager to the project board, not from the team manager.
A checkpoint report is the agreed regular team-to-project-manager progress report for a work package.
This is produced at a stage boundary rather than every week for work-package delivery.
An exception report concerns a forecast tolerance breach and is not a normal periodic team update.

questions.stem: The project manager needs to summarize stage progress at agreed intervals for the project board. Which report is most appropriate?
questions.why: The project manager uses highlight reports to keep the board informed on stage progress at regular intervals.
optionWhy: Checkpoint reports are usually sent by team managers to the project manager.
An issue report gives formal information on a particular issue, not a regular stage progress summary.
The project manager uses highlight reports to keep the board informed on stage progress at regular intervals.
An end project report evaluates total project performance at closure, not periodic stage progress.

questions.stem: The forecast finish date breaches the stage time tolerance even though the date has not yet arrived. How should this be treated?
options: Wait until the actual late finish before reporting
Ask the team to ignore the agreed tolerance
Change the approved stage baseline without authority
Escalate the forecast stage exception to the project board
questions.why: A forecast outside stage tolerance requires the project manager to raise an exception report.
optionWhy: PRINCE2 escalation is triggered by a forecast breach, not only a realized failure.
Tolerances define delegated authority and cannot simply be disregarded.
An unauthorized baseline change is not an appropriate response to forecast exception.
A forecast outside stage tolerance requires the project manager to raise an exception report.

questions.stem: Which control is event-driven rather than time-driven?
options: The board authorization of the next stage
questions.why: Stage-end authorization occurs at a defined event, not an agreed regular time interval.
optionWhy: Stage-end authorization occurs at a defined event, not an agreed regular time interval.
A checkpoint report can be produced at predetermined intervals, so it is time-driven.
Regular reports at predefined time intervals are time-driven controls.
A report at a fixed daily interval is time-driven even if delivered by email.

questions.stem: A team manager predicts a work package will breach tolerance. What should the team manager do initially?
options: Send an exception report directly to the project board
Raise an issue with the project manager
Wait for a formal end project report
questions.why: The team manager refers a forecast work-package breach to the project manager for a decision.
optionWhy: Stage-level exception reports are normally prepared by the project manager for the board.
The team manager refers a forecast work-package breach to the project manager for a decision.
Work-package and project tolerances are delegated from higher management levels.
That report is not relevant to managing the current work package exception.

questions.stem: What does the end project report primarily enable?
options: Routine delegation of a new work package
The project manager’s weekly status communication
Evaluation of completed project performance against agreed baselines
Automatic confirmation of all benefits scheduled after closure
questions.why: The end project report supports closure with a view of achievement, variances, benefits and lessons.
optionWhy: Work packages are authorized during controlling a stage, not via project closure reporting.
Periodic stage communications use highlight reports.
The end project report supports closure with a view of achievement, variances, benefits and lessons.
Benefits can be realized later and must be reviewed as planned.

questions.stem: Which product is best for recording an informal day-to-day matter that the project manager can handle without formal escalation?
questions.why: The daily log can capture informal issues, reminders and other day-to-day matters.
optionWhy: An issue report is used for issues warranting formal handling and analysis.
This is for forecast tolerance breaches, not every small matter.
A product register lists products and status, not the running record of informal issues.
The daily log can capture informal issues, reminders and other day-to-day matters.

questions.stem: A project needs an agreed plan for how project information is captured, stored, protected and used in reporting. Which PID approach is most relevant?
questions.why: This approach sets how digital information and data will be managed for reliable project control.
optionWhy: This approach sets how digital information and data will be managed for reliable project control.
This concerns outcomes, benefit measurements and reviews, not project data governance generally.
This concerns procurement and business-supplier relationships, not overall project data arrangements.
This defines quality methods and responsibilities, not data governance across project controls.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a forecast and a tolerance?
options: A forecast is an approved baseline; tolerance is the daily log
A forecast predicts an outcome; tolerance defines the permitted deviation
Both are names for a stage plan
Tolerance predicts the completion date; forecast grants authority
questions.why: Comparing forecasts with tolerances allows managers to detect possible exceptions early.
optionWhy: A forecast predicts performance, while tolerance defines permitted deviation from targets.
Comparing forecasts with tolerances allows managers to detect possible exceptions early.
A stage plan includes targets and may contain tolerances, but forecast is a prediction about likely results.
The roles are reversed: forecasts estimate and tolerances bound delegated authority.

questions.stem:
Which two reports are normally time-driven?
1. Checkpoint report.
2. Exception report.
3. Highlight report.
4. End stage report.
questions.why: Checkpoint and highlight reports are typically produced at agreed intervals.
optionWhy: Checkpoint reports are regular, but exception reports arise because of a forecast breach.
Checkpoint and highlight reports are typically produced at agreed intervals.
Exception and end stage reports are linked to events rather than regular intervals.
Highlight reports are regular, but end stage reports occur at a stage boundary.

questions.stem: A business asks whether a proposed project is worth investigating, before funding detailed initiation. Which process supports this decision?
questions.why: Starting up prepares the outline case and brief to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.
optionWhy: Initiating develops the detailed foundations after permission to initiate, not the initial pre-project check.
Starting up prepares the outline case and brief to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.
Stage boundary review supports decisions about later stages, not whether to begin initiation.
Closure confirms acceptance and orderly finish rather than testing the initial mandate.

questions.stem: Which process gives the project board authority to authorize initiation, delivery stages and closure?
questions.why: The board’s process makes major authorization and direction decisions throughout the lifecycle.
optionWhy: The project manager controls stage delivery; the board makes key authorizations elsewhere.
Team managers accept and deliver work packages, not approve the overall project.
The board’s process makes major authorization and direction decisions throughout the lifecycle.
Initiation creates the baseline and evidence for authorization; directing makes the approval decision.

questions.stem: What is the central result of initiating a project before substantial delivery investment?
options: A guaranteed complete benefit realization report
Only a list of potential suppliers
A credible set of foundations and project initiation documentation
questions.why: Initiation develops enough business, plan, quality and control information for the board to decide on delivery.
optionWhy: Benefits may occur later; initiation cannot prove them in advance.
The final product is delivered later; initiation establishes how it will be achieved.
Supplier information is useful but does not make a complete project baseline.
Initiation develops enough business, plan, quality and control information for the board to decide on delivery.

questions.stem: A project manager authorizes a work package and monitors the stage’s progress. Which process is being used?
questions.why: The project manager delegates, monitors and takes corrective action during a stage.
optionWhy: Stage boundaries prepare information for the next stage, not daily authorization of work packages.
The project manager delegates, monitors and takes corrective action during a stage.
The project board exercises overall control and authorizes stages, not every routine work package.
Closure confirms acceptance and handover after delivery.

questions.stem: A team manager agrees a work package with the project manager, executes it and returns completed products. Which process describes this?
questions.why: Team managers use this process to accept, execute and deliver agreed product work.
optionWhy: Team managers use this process to accept, execute and deliver agreed product work.
The project manager uses this process to authorize work and monitor stage delivery.
This prepares plans and reports for future stage authorization.
This is the project board’s direction and authorization process.

questions.stem: Near the end of a stage, the project manager updates the overall plan and prepares a detailed next-stage plan. Which process is being used?
questions.why: This process prepares the next stage plan and updated evidence for board decisions.
optionWhy: Starting up happens before initiation and creates initial project definition, not future stage plans.
Closure evaluates and hands over the whole project; this scenario concerns continuing into another stage.
This process prepares the next stage plan and updated evidence for board decisions.
The team manager controls completion of work packages, not stage transitions.

questions.stem: The final product has been accepted. The project manager evaluates performance and asks the board to authorize closure. Which process is central?
questions.why: The process confirms acceptance, handover, evaluation and orderly closure or premature closure.
optionWhy: Initiation prepares the project baseline before delivery, not its closure evaluation.
Stage control may manage the final stage, but closure provides the fixed acceptance and handover point.
Stage boundary review supports continuation decisions; this is the final close.
The process confirms acceptance, handover, evaluation and orderly closure or premature closure.

questions.stem: Which process operates across the entire project, even as the project manager moves through several stages?
questions.why: The project board’s directing process spans authorization, stage decisions and closure across the project lifecycle.
optionWhy: Work package delivery repeats during relevant stages but is not the board’s overarching process.
The project board’s directing process spans authorization, stage decisions and closure across the project lifecycle.
Starting up is pre-project and precedes authorization of initiation.
Closing occurs near the end or during premature closure, not continuously throughout stages.

questions.stem: During starting up a project, what is normally prepared to plan the work needed for the next process?
options: Team plan for every specialist group
questions.why: The initiation stage plan sets the work and resources needed to create the PID and other initiation products.
optionWhy: The initiation stage plan sets the work and resources needed to create the PID and other initiation products.
This compares results at closure, long after starting up.
An exception plan would only be needed after an approved plan is forecast to breach tolerance.
Team plans may be optional and are not all mandatory pre-project products.

questions.stem: After starting up, the project manager asks for permission to enter initiation. Which process handles the board’s authorization?
questions.why: The project board authorizes initiation through its directing process.
optionWhy: The initial initiation stage is authorized after start-up through board direction, not at a subsequent boundary.
Initiating follows authorization to initiate and prepares the case for authorizing delivery.
The project board authorizes initiation through its directing process.
Closure does not authorize the start of initiation.

questions.stem: A completed work package has been returned by a team manager. In which process will the project manager normally review it for stage progress?
questions.why: The project manager reviews completed work and monitors stage progress in controlling a stage.
optionWhy: Stage boundaries summarize stage results for the board; routine work package review is stage control.
The project manager reviews completed work and monitors stage progress in controlling a stage.
The board receives overall progress information; it does not normally inspect every work package.
Starting up happens before detailed delivery work begins.

questions.stem: An exception report has been considered and the board requests a replacement stage plan. Where is that replacement developed?
questions.why: An exception plan can be prepared under managing a stage boundary when directed by the board.
optionWhy: An exception plan can be prepared under managing a stage boundary when directed by the board.
The team delivers authorized work packages, not a board-requested replacement stage plan.
The scenario concerns continuation with a revised stage rather than closure.
Starting up is the pre-initiation work, not exception recovery during delivery.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words. The purpose of ______ is to control the link between the project manager and team manager for specialist products.
questions.why: This process agrees requirements for accepting, executing, reporting and delivering work-package products.
optionWhy: Directing is the board’s overall control and authorization process.
Controlling a stage is where the project manager authorizes and monitors team work, but the team interface is the delivery process.
Stage boundaries prepare next-stage authorization information, not routine team acceptance and delivery.
This process agrees requirements for accepting, executing, reporting and delivering work-package products.

questions.stem: A project is being terminated early because its remaining costs cannot be justified. Which statement best describes proper management?
options: Abandon all remaining records and transfer staff immediately
Use closing a project to perform an orderly premature close
Continue spending until the original final date regardless of value
Authorize new delivery work packages without reviewing the decision
questions.why: PRINCE2’s closure process supports both normal and premature closure with appropriate review and handover.
optionWhy: An orderly close still needs to record results, address open issues, and hand over appropriate information.
PRINCE2’s closure process supports both normal and premature closure with appropriate review and handover.
Continued business justification requires action when investment is no longer warranted.
More delivery work would conflict with the board’s closure direction.

questions.stem:
Which two process statements are correct?
1. Directing a project provides board-level control.
2. Starting up a project creates the detailed PID.
3. Initiating a project prepares the project’s detailed foundations.
4. Managing product delivery authorizes all management stages.
questions.why: Directing makes key board decisions; initiating establishes the detailed case, plan and controls.
optionWhy: Directing is board-level, but starting up prepares the brief and outline case rather than the detailed PID.
Starting up does not create the detailed PID, and stage authorization is a directing-level decision.
Directing makes key board decisions; initiating establishes the detailed case, plan and controls.
Initiation develops the foundations, but managing product delivery does not authorize stages.

questions.stem: Which process confirms that acceptance of the overall project product is formally recognized?
questions.why: Closing provides the fixed point for confirmation of overall project product acceptance.
optionWhy: This process concerns individual work-package products and team delivery, not overall project closure acceptance.
A stage boundary reviews stage completion and prepares continuation information, not the final overall acceptance point.
Starting up captures initial expectations; acceptance occurs after the product is delivered.
Closing provides the fixed point for confirmation of overall project product acceptance.

questions.stem: A project has two technical workstreams proceeding concurrently. What does PRINCE2 require of management stages?
options: The two management stages must overlap exactly like the technical workstreams
Management stages form sequential governance periods, even if technical work overlaps
There can be no more than one management stage
Each technical skill must have its own separate management stage
questions.why: Technical teams may work concurrently while board control is structured by management stage boundaries.
optionWhy: Technical and management stages serve different purposes; management stages do not overlap.
Technical teams may work concurrently while board control is structured by management stage boundaries.
PRINCE2 requires at least initiation and one subsequent management stage.
Technical specialization does not dictate a one-to-one relationship with management stages.

questions.stem:
The project board requests an updated overall viability assessment at the end of a stage. Which two outputs are most relevant?
1. End stage report.
2. Next stage plan.
3. Team members’ personal calendars only.
4. Unapproved supplier change requests only.
questions.why: The end stage report and next stage plan help the board judge past progress and the next commitment.
optionWhy: The end stage report and next stage plan help the board judge past progress and the next commitment.
The end stage report helps, but personal calendars alone do not define the next delivery commitment.
The next stage plan matters, but unapproved supplier proposals alone do not give a full stage assessment.
Neither personal calendars nor unapproved proposals replaces stage performance and planning information.

questions.stem: A project manager must send a completed PID to the board for a delivery authorization decision. Which process has just provided that information?
questions.why: Initiation assembles the PID for the project board’s later authorization decision under directing a project.
optionWhy: Closure evaluates the delivered project; the PID supports authorizing delivery before it begins.
The delivery process produces specialist products under work packages, not the PID baseline.
Initiation assembles the PID for the project board’s later authorization decision under directing a project.
Starting up prepares the brief and initiation request rather than the full PID.
